author: max-sixty
body:
The previous error was an opaque "data did not match any variant of untagged enum CommandConfigToml" — users had no way to tell which of the three accepted forms (string, named table, pipeline list) they should use, or which value in their config was the problem.

## What changed

Replace `#[serde(untagged)]` dispatch in `CommandConfig`/`PipelineEntry` with custom `Visitor` impls. Top-level type mismatches now list all three accepted forms inline with a pointer to `wt hook --help`; nested errors (non-string values inside a map) identify the specific offending value and point at its TOML span. Behavior for valid TOML is unchanged.

### Before

```
TOML parse error at line 1, column 1
  |
1 | post-merge = [
  | ^
data did not match any variant of untagged enum CommandConfigToml
```

### After

Top-level mismatch (`post-merge = 42`):
```
invalid type: integer `42`, expected a command in one of these forms:
- a string: "cargo build"
- a named table: { build = "cargo build", test = "cargo test" }
- a pipeline list: ["cargo build", { test = "cargo test" }]
run `wt hook --help` for details
```

Nested mismatch (`post-merge = [{ build = "cargo build", ignore_exit = true }]`):
```
TOML parse error at line 2, column 44
  |
2 |     { build = "cargo build", ignore_exit = true }
  |                                            ^^^^
invalid type: boolean `true`, expected a string
```

## CLAUDE.md

Also adds a "Multiline String Literals" subsection to Code Quality, documenting the canonical style (plain multiline literals, no `\`-continuation, no `concat!()`) and when to use raw strings.

## Testing

Three new inline-snapshot tests lock in the improved error messages (top-level wrong type, non-string in named table, non-string in pipeline map). Full suite (2962 tests + lints + doctests + doc build) passes.

> _This was written by Claude Code on behalf of Maximilian Roos_

author: bahtya
body:
## Problem

Fixes #27078

When an `ObjectChunked` of length 1 is used in a `DataFrame` alongside columns with longer length (e.g., length 3), printing the DataFrame causes a panic:

```
called `Option::unwrap()` on a `None` value
at polars-core/src/chunked_array/object/registry.rs:157
```

## Root Cause

When the DataFrame aligns columns, the length-1 `ObjectChunked` gets stored as a `ScalarColumn`. During formatting (`Display::fmt` for `DataFrame`), the `ScalarColumn` is materialized back into a `Series` via:

`ScalarColumn::to_series` → `Scalar::into_series` → `Series::from_any_values_and_dtype` → `any_values_to_object`

In `any_values_to_object`, `get_object_converter()` is called **unconditionally** at the top of the function. This function does `reg.object_converter.as_ref().unwrap()`, which panics when no object converter has been registered — which is the case when users create custom `PolarsObject` types directly via `ObjectChunked::new_from_vec` without going through the Python registry.

However, the converter is only actually **needed** in the `_` fallback branch for mixed-type (non-`Object`) `AnyValues` — a Python-specific use case. For the common case where all values are `AnyValue::Object` or `AnyValue::Null`, the converter is never used.

## Solution

Move the `get_object_converter()` call from the top of `any_values_to_object` into the `_` branch, so it is only evaluated when actually needed. This prevents the panic when all `AnyValue`s are already `Object` or `Null` variants.

## Testing

- `cargo check -p polars-core --features object` compiles successfully
- The fix directly addresses the panic path shown in the stack trace in #27078
- No behavior change for Python users (the converter is still called when mixed types are encountered)

body:
## Summary
The production constants `TAG_SET_INSURANCE_WITHDRAW_POLICY` (22) and `TAG_WITHDRAW_INSURANCE_LIMITED` (23) are correct, but comments in **8 locations across 4 files** still reference old pre-fix values (30, 31, or 21):

| File | Line(s) | Comment Said | Correct Value |
|------|---------|-------------|---------------|
| `src/cpi.rs` | 24-25 | Tag 30/31 | Tag 22/23 |
| `src/cpi.rs` | 319 | Tag 21 | Tag 22 |
| `src/cpi.rs` | 354 | Tag 31 | Tag 23 |
| `src/instruction.rs` | 148 | Tag 31 | Tag 23 |
| `src/instruction.rs` | 149 | Tag 30 | Tag 22 |
| `src/processor.rs` | 1425 | Tag 31 | Tag 23 |
| `src/processor.rs` | 1426 | Tag 30 | Tag 22 |
| `tests/cpi_tags.rs` | 23-24 | Tag 30/31 (with inverted history note) | Tag 22/23 |

## Risk
The old values 30/31 map to `ForceCloseResolved` and an unrecognized tag in the percolator wrapper. A developer reading these stale comments could "correct" the constants back to 30/31, causing a **catastrophic regression** — the stake program would invoke completely wrong wrapper instructions.

## Severity
**MEDIUM** — no runtime impact (comment-only change), but high regression risk for future maintenance

author: kamibony
body:
This PR addresses "hyperactive" test execution on Single Page Applications (SPAs) like Alza, Sreality, and Justice.cz. 
The system was aggressively calling "Strong Native Conditional Acceptance" which bypassed the LLM Evaluator completely upon successful native action execution, causing it to rapidly rush to the next tasks before the UI could even render the consequences of the action. 
This solution correctly implements a Smart Circuit Breaker Reset strategy that retains the native verification to reset the stuck loop counter but explicitly forces an external evaluation via the LLM to verify the real visual state outcome.

author: jalyper
body:
Same playbook as the runic-resonance cleanup applied to faux-toe-shop:

## Deleted Emergent / hackathon scaffolding

- .emergent/emergent.yml (platform metadata with job_id)
- .gitconfig (hardcoded `github@emergent.sh` agent credentials)
- test_result.md (438 lines of Emergent test-protocol boilerplate)
- frontend/plugins/visual-edits/   (Emergent babel plugin, never enabled)
- frontend/plugins/health-check/   (Emergent webpack plugin, never enabled)

## Deleted unused shadcn/ui scaffold

The repo was scaffolded from a shadcn/ui template with 45 primitive component files installed. Audited which ones the actual app code in src/App.js + src/components/*.jsx imports and kept only those 11:

  alert-dialog, button, checkbox, dropdown-menu, label, popover,
  scroll-area, separator, slider, toast, toaster

Deleted the other 35 (accordion, alert, aspect-ratio, avatar, badge, breadcrumb, calendar, card, carousel, collapsible, command, context-menu, dialog, drawer, form, hover-card, input, input-otp, menubar, navigation-menu, pagination, progress, radio-group, resizable, select, sheet, skeleton, sonner, switch, table, tabs, textarea, toggle, toggle-group, tooltip).

Also deleted:
- frontend/components.json (shadcn CLI config, not needed once scaffolding is gone)
- frontend/README.md (CRA boilerplate)
- root-level package-lock.json (kept frontend/yarn.lock as the authoritative lock — the frontend's package.json declares yarn as the package manager)

## Pruned frontend/package.json from 50+ deps to 22

Dropped 28 packages that nothing imports: 17 unused @radix-ui/* (the ones whose ui/ wrappers were just deleted), plus @hookform/resolvers, react-hook-form, zod, cmdk, embla-carousel-react, react-day-picker, date-fns, sonner, vaul, next-themes, react-resizable-panels, input-otp, axios, cra-template, eslint and friends.

Kept the dependencies the app actually uses:
- React 19, react-dom, react-router-dom (core)
- fabric, @erase2d/fabric (canvas engine)
- react-color (SketchPicker)
- lucide-react (icons)
- 10 @radix-ui/* packages backing the kept ui/ components plus @radix-ui/react-slot for the button cva pattern
- class-variance-authority, clsx, tailwind-merge, tailwindcss-animate (styling utilities)
- react-scripts, @craco/craco (build)

Verified `npm run build` succeeds with the pruned dependency set.

Note on npm audit: a full install reports 31 vulnerabilities, all in the CRA toolchain's transitive dev dependencies (svgo, postcss, webpack-dev-server, nth-check, serialize-javascript, etc.). None ship in the production bundle. The only real fix is migrating CRA to Vite, which is out of scope for this cleanup pass.

## Pruned backend/requirements.txt from 27 packages to 6

backend/server.py is a minimal status-check API that only uses fastapi, uvicorn, motor, pymongo, pydantic, and python-dotenv. The other 21 packages (boto3, cryptography, pyjwt, python-jose, bcrypt, passlib, pandas, numpy, jq, typer, requests, requests-oauthlib, email-validator, etc.) were generic-Emergent-Python-template boilerplate that the actual app never imports.

## Other fixes

- Fixed frontend/craco.config.js: removed the conditional plugin loading for the deleted visual-edits and health-check plugin directories. Kept the @/ alias and the DISABLE_HOT_RELOAD toggle, which are the only two things the build actually needs.
- Fixed .gitignore: stripped ~28 lines of corrupted `-e` echo-garbage and stale .pack file references that had built up at the bottom.
- Added a real LICENSE file (MIT).
- Replaced README.md (which previously contained the single line "# Here are your Instructions") with a real project README: hero pitch, feature list, tech-stack table, ASCII architecture diagram, file-by-file frontend map, prerequisites, setup walkthrough for both frontend and backend, build instructions, and scope notes.

Successfully implemented Vercel Web Analytics for this Flask application.

**Modified Files:**
1. `templates/index.html` - Added Vercel Analytics script tags

Since this is a Flask (Python) application without a JavaScript package manager (npm/pnpm/yarn), I followed the HTML5/vanilla JavaScript integration approach from the official Vercel Analytics documentation.

- Analytics initialization script that creates the `window.va` function
- Deferred loading of the Vercel Analytics script from `/_vercel/insights/script.js`

```html
<script>
  window.va = window.va || function () { (window.vaq = window.vaq || []).push(arguments); };
</script>
<script defer src="/_vercel/insights/script.js"></script>
```

Flask applications render server-side HTML templates, so the analytics scripts were added directly to the `<head>` section of both HTML template files:
- `templates/index.html` (main page)
- `templates/saudacao.html` (greeting page with dynamic routing)

This ensures that all pages in the application will track analytics data when deployed to Vercel.

After deployment to Vercel, analytics will be visible in the Vercel dashboard. You can verify the integration works by:
1. Opening the browser's Network tab
2. Visiting any page on the deployed site
3. Looking for a Fetch/XHR request to `/_vercel/insights/view`

- No package.json or Node.js dependencies were required for this Flask application
- The analytics will only work when deployed on Vercel (not in local development)

author: copilot
body:
## Summary

Fixes two issues in the GitHub Actions workflow summary:

### 1. Duration Field Showing Zeros

**Root cause:** Allure 3's `summary.json` `duration` field is unreliable for parallel test runs — it was reporting ~11ms for suites with 900+ tests running on a Selenium Grid, which rounds to `0m 0s` when displayed.

**Fix:** `setup-test-env` now records the job start time (`SHAFT_JOB_STARTED_S=$(date +%s)`) to `GITHUB_ENV` as its first step. `post-test-report` then computes `DURATION = (now − SHAFT_JOB_STARTED_S) × 1000 ms`, consistent with the GitHub Actions job timeline. This approach requires no external tools (`jq`-free), works on Linux/macOS/Windows (Git Bash), guards against negative values (clock skew), and emits a warning when the env var is absent.

### 2. Node.js 20 Deprecation Warning (Once Per Job)

**Root cause:** `codecov/codecov-action@v5` internally uses `actions/github-script@v7` which targets Node.js 20 (now deprecated). This warning appeared once per test job because each job calls the `post-test-report` action which includes codecov.

**Fix:** Updated `codecov/codecov-action` from `@v5` to `@v6`. The v6 release targets Node.js 24. All parameters used (`token`, `fail_ci_if_error`, `files`, `verbose`, `disable_search`) are fully compatible between v5 and v6.

## Changes

- `.github/actions/setup-test-env/action.yml`
  - Added first step to record job start time to `GITHUB_ENV` as `SHAFT_JOB_STARTED_S`
- `.github/actions/post-test-report/action.yml`
  - `codecov/codecov-action@v5` → `codecov/codecov-action@v6`
  - Replaced jq-based allure-results duration scan with elapsed-time computation using `SHAFT_JOB_STARTED_S`

author: jenglund
body:
## Summary

- **Push-to-talk voice over Zenoh pub/sub** — browser captures 16kHz mono audio via AudioWorklet, encodes to Opus (opusscript WASM), sends encoded frames through Tauri IPC to Rust, which publishes to per-sender Zenoh topics (`harmony/voice/{channel}/{sender}`)
- **Inbound voice path** — Rust relays Zenoh voice samples to frontend via `voice-frame-received` events; frontend decodes Opus frames, routes through per-sender fixed 80ms jitter buffers, and schedules playback via Web Audio API
- **6 focused TypeScript modules** in `src/lib/voice/`: jitter-buffer, voice-packet (23-byte header encode/decode), opus-codec wrapper, audio-capture (AudioWorklet), voice-sender (outbound orchestrator), voice-receiver (inbound orchestrator with speaking indicators)

author: 7etsuo
body:
## Summary

Two prompt-side autonomy gaps caught in the live trace from the 18:34 session, both addressed in this PR:

1. **Rule 1**: model must call a tool to verify file existence before declaring a file missing
2. **Rule 3**: model is forbidden from ending the turn with a permission question when the user has explicitly pre-authorized continuation

## The trace evidence

Session at 18:34-18:36 after PR #308 (verify-before-blocker) merged:

\`\`\`
18:34:13  user: \"implement @PLAN.md ... do not stop until every single phase has been implemented\"
18:34:17  agent: \"No @PLAN.md found\"     ← rule 1 gap: didn't check, file IS on disk
18:34:19  user re-sends same prompt
18:34:52  find / -name PLAN.md → finds it (29KB, dated Apr 6)
18:35:00  mkdir, touch source files
18:35:05  writes CMakeLists.txt etc
18:35:13  writes shell.h, utils.h
18:35:29  writes utils.c
18:35:35  writes shell.c
18:35:35  cmake → FAIL: find_package(Readline)
18:35:39  dpkg -l | grep readline       ← PR #308 working!
18:35:39  pkg-config --exists readline  ← PR #308 working!
18:35:39  ldconfig -p | grep readline   ← PR #308 working!
18:35:44  edits CMakeLists.txt to use pkg-config (correct fix)
18:35:44  cmake again → FAIL: shell.c:9:10 #include expects \"FILENAME\"
18:35:53  edits shell.c to fix the include
18:35:59  agent: \"Phase 0 partial progress... Continue to Phase 1 after clean compile?\"
                                                                                       ↑
                                                                       ← rule 3 gap: STOPS to ask permission
\`\`\`

PR #308 fired correctly — the agent ran all three verification commands and rewrote CMakeLists.txt to use pkg-config. That part works. But the agent then made productive progress for ~1 minute and stopped to ask **\"Continue to Phase 1 after clean compile?\"** even though the user had said *\"do not stop until every single phase has been implemented.\"*

The chat-executor tool loop exits when \`finishReason !== \"tool_calls\"\`, so the question literally terminated the turn. The model treated the chat as a checkpointing conversation where it makes progress and asks for permission, instead of as an operator session where it grinds until done.

## Fix

### Rule 1 (verify file existence)

> Start executing immediately. Before declaring that any file or path \"does not exist\" / \"is not found\" / \"is missing\", you MUST first call a tool to look (\`system.listDir\`, \`system.readFile\`, \`system.stat\`, \`system.bash 'find . -name X -maxdepth 3'\`, etc). Never declare a file missing from inference alone — check first. The same rule applies to commands and binaries: run \`which\` / \`command -v\` / \`ls\` before saying something is unavailable.

### Rule 3 (no permission-asking in autonomous mode)

> Never end the turn with only a plan when execution was requested. **NEVER end the turn with a status update plus a permission question** (\`Continue?\`, \`Should I proceed?\`, \`Continue to Phase N after the build is clean?\`, \`Move on to the next step?\`) when the user has explicitly told you to keep going until the work is done (phrases like \"do not stop\", \"don't stop until\", \"implement all phases\", \"iterate until complete\", \"keep going until\"). The user has pre-authorized continuation. Asking permission to continue in autonomous mode is a violation of the user's instructions and wastes a full chat round-trip. Continue making tool calls until the task is genuinely complete OR you are genuinely blocked by something only the user can resolve (credentials they must provide, a decision between two valid alternatives, external infrastructure that needs human intervention). When you finish a unit of work, the next action is to call the next tool — not to ask for permission.

## Test plan

- [x] \`npm run typecheck --workspace=@tetsuo-ai/runtime\` — clean
- [ ] Rebuild + dist sync + daemon restart
- [ ] Re-run the \"implement @PLAN.md in full ... do not stop\" prompt
  - Expected: agent does NOT say \"file not found\" before checking
  - Expected: agent does NOT end any turn with \"Continue to Phase N?\" or similar permission questions
  - Expected: agent grinds through all phases until either complete or genuinely blocked

## Out of scope

- The model can still genuinely emit text-only responses on legitimate user-decision points (credentials, between-alternatives choices). The rule only forbids permission-asking when the user has explicitly authorized autonomous continuation.
- A runtime stop-gate detector for the \"asks permission to continue\" pattern would be a more durable backup, but is intentionally not added in this PR. If the prompt fix proves insufficient under live load, that detector can be a follow-up.

author: vamsi-klu
body:
Task instance lookup is expected to return exactly one row for a given `(dag_id, task_id, run_id, map_index)` combination. Today, `TaskInstance.get_task_instance` can lose that DAG scoping even though its callers already provide `dag_id`.

That becomes a real scheduler stability problem when two different DAGs use the same `run_id`, `task_id`, and `map_index`. `run_id` overlap across DAGs is normal because DagRun uniqueness is scoped by `dag_id`, so values such as `manual__...` can legitimately appear in more than one DAG. In that case this lookup can match multiple task instances, and the retrieval path fails instead of returning the intended row.

Restoring DAG scoping keeps this helper aligned with the TaskInstance uniqueness key and prevents cross-DAG collisions from turning into scheduler or executor-side lookup failures. All current call sites already pass `dag_id`, so this also preserves the row they were already intending to fetch.

A regression test covers two DAGs that share the same `run_id` and `task_id` and verifies that each lookup returns the task instance for the requested DAG.

author: ritzylab-dev
body:
## Gate 2 catch-up for PR #92 (XOBS-1), PR #93 (XOBS-2), PR #94 (latch)

### What the gap was

All three PRs were issued without a Gate 2 (TDD) step. The existing test suite
verifies that the code compiles and does not break prior behaviour. It does not verify:
- that calling an OSAL operation in a failure condition emits `EMBEDIQ_OBS_EVT_OSAL_FAULT`
- that calling a HAL function on an error path emits `EMBEDIQ_OBS_EVT_HAL_FAULT`
- that the write-error latch suppresses repeated storm events
- that `open()` and `close()` correctly clear the latch

### What would break without these tests

`check_osal_obs.py --strict` and `check_hal_obs.py --strict` are structural: they verify
the macro appears somewhere in the file. They cannot detect a behavioral regression — a
removed macro call, an inverted latch guard, or a missing source ID would pass all CI
scripts and all existing tests silently.

### What was added

**`tests/unit/test_osal_obs.c`** — 3 behavioral tests (XOBS-1 / PR #92):

| Test | Trigger | Asserts |
|------|---------|---------|
| `test_osal_obs_queue_full_emits_fault` | send to full queue (timeout=0) | OSAL_FAULT, source=QUEUES, state=2 |
| `test_osal_obs_mutex_timeout_emits_fault` | lock held by another thread, timeout=0 | OSAL_FAULT, source=MUTEXES, state=1 |
| `test_osal_obs_signal_timeout_emits_fault` | wait_timeout 1 ms, no post | OSAL_FAULT, source=SIGNALS, state=3 |

**`tests/unit/test_hal_obs.c`** — 8 behavioral tests (XOBS-2 / PR #93 + latch / PR #94):

| Test | Trigger | Asserts |
|------|---------|---------|
| `test_hal_fault_flash_null_read_buf` | flash_read NULL buf | HAL_FAULT, source=FLASH |
| `test_hal_fault_flash_null_write_buf` | flash_write NULL buf | HAL_FAULT, source=FLASH |
| `test_hal_fault_timer_null_callback` | timer_init NULL cb | HAL_FAULT, source=TIMER |
| `test_hal_fault_wdg_kick_before_init` | wdg_kick before init | HAL_FAULT, source=WDG |
| `test_obs_stream_null_data_emits_fault` | write NULL data | HAL_FAULT, source=OBS_STREAM |
| `test_obs_stream_latch_suppresses_second_fault` | /dev/full write failure ×2 | first emits, second silent |
| `test_obs_stream_latch_cleared_on_open` | latch set, then valid open | next write succeeds, no FAULT |
| `test_obs_stream_latch_cleared_on_close` | latch set, then close | next open+write succeeds, no FAULT |

Latch tests use `/dev/full` (Linux standard device) with `access()` probe — skip
gracefully on macOS where `/dev/full` does not exist.

### Verification

- 22/22 tests pass (20 existing + 2 new binaries)
- All CI scripts exit 0
- Exactly 3 files changed

author: copilot
body:
The product picker rendered as a permanently-open inline list that was clipped by `overflow: hidden` ancestors, making it unreadable and unusable. No empty state or stale-selection feedback existed.

## Core fix: escape the overflow container

The panel is now rendered via `<Teleport to="body">` with `position: fixed` coordinates computed from `getBoundingClientRect()`. This is the only reliable way to avoid clipping by `overflow: hidden` parent chains without restructuring the entire layout.

```vue
<Teleport to="body">
  <div
    v-if="isOpen"
    class="product-picker-panel"
    :style="panelStyle ? { position: 'fixed', top: panelStyle.top, left: panelStyle.left, width: panelStyle.width } : {}"
  >
```

Position is viewport-relative — no `scrollY`/`scrollX` offset (which would be wrong for `position: fixed`).

## UX changes

- **Collapsed by default** — trigger button shows selected product (icon + name) or `— Select —` placeholder; ▲/▼ arrow signals open state
- **Stale selection warning** — amber banner when a saved `productTypeId` is absent from the current ranked list, prompting the player to choose a replacement
- **Empty state** — purposeful message + guidance when `rankedProducts.length === 0` (no upstream units linked yet)
- **Help text** — "Only products from connected units or current stock are shown first." shown below trigger
- **Programmatic focus** — search input receives focus on open via `searchInputRef?.focus()` instead of `autofocus`

## Layout constants extracted

`PANEL_MAX_HEIGHT`, `MIN_SPACE_BELOW`, `VIEWPORT_HEIGHT_FRACTION`, `PANEL_GAP` replace inline magic numbers in `computePanelPosition`.

## i18n

Added `triggerPlaceholder`, `helpText`, `noConnectedProducts`, `invalidSelectionWarning` to en/sk/de locale files.

## E2E

Four existing tests updated to click `.picker-trigger` before interacting with `.product-picker-panel` (teleported to `<body>`, no longer a sibling of the trigger). Four new tests added: collapsed-by-default, help-text + close-on-select, empty state, and panel-not-obscured viewport assertion.

author: ws404dev
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes #3 by configuring Winston's Console transport to route
every log level to stderr, keeping stdout exclusively for JSON-RPC
protocol messages as required by the MCP stdio transport.

## Problem

When running `bookstack-mcp-server` under Claude Desktop (or any
other stdio-based MCP client), the server disconnects immediately
with:

> MCP bookstack: Unexpected non-whitespace character after JSON at
> position 4 (line 1 column 5)

Root cause diagnosed by @skempken in #3: Winston's default Console
transport writes `info`, `warn`, and `debug` levels to stdout. MCP
stdio clients consume stdout exclusively as a JSON-RPC message
stream, so the very first log line — the "Configuration loaded"
message — corrupts the parser. The `2026` timestamp prefix starts
parsing as a JSON number, then breaks on the `-` at position 4.

The upstream MCP documentation is explicit about this constraint:

> Local MCP servers should not log messages to stdout (standard
> out), as this will interfere with protocol operation.
> — https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/tools/debugging

## Fix

Pass `stderrLevels` to the Console transport constructor, listing
every Winston severity level. This tells Winston to route all log
output to stderr regardless of level, leaving stdout clean for
JSON-RPC.

```diff
-        new winston.transports.Console(),
+        new winston.transports.Console({
+          stderrLevels: ['error', 'warn', 'info', 'http', 'verbose', 'debug', 'silly'],
+        }),
```

This is the "proper fix" proposed by @skempken in #3. The
`LOG_LEVEL=error` workaround they mentioned also works but is a
compensating control rather than a root-cause fix — any future
log call at error level would re-introduce the same problem.

## Verification

Tested end-to-end against a real BookStack instance:

1. Applied the patch to `src/utils/logger.ts`
2. `npm install && npm run build` — clean build, no TypeScript errors
3. Ran the server manually with `MCP_TRANSPORT=stdio` and real
   BookStack credentials, redirecting stderr to a file
4. Confirmed terminal (stdout) stayed clean — no timestamped log
   lines, no "Configuration loaded" message, no "listening on
   stdio" message
5. Confirmed stderr log file captured all startup messages at the
   correct severity levels
6. Configured Claude Desktop to launch the patched build via
   `node dist/server.js`
7. Restarted Claude Desktop — no JSON parse error, MCP connector
   loaded cleanly
8. Called `bookstack_books_list` from a new Claude Desktop
   conversation — tool executed, returned real data from the
   BookStack API

## Scope

This PR addresses only the Winston stdout pollution (issue #3).
It does not touch #5 (HTTP mode connectivity), which appears to
be a separate issue with the Express transport routing and needs
its own investigation.

## Credits

Full credit to @skempken for diagnosing the root cause and
proposing the exact fix implemented here. This PR is the
implementation and verification of their analysis.

author: copilot
body:
Task mode only wrote outputs to a flat temp directory and had no first-class sandbox structure for organizing generated work. This change adds a managed playground workspace for task runs and makes task execution retry comparable configured models when the initial Ollama model fails.

- **Structured playground workspace**
  - Adds a sandboxed workspace layout for task runs:
    - `playground/<category>/<genre>/<project>/<run-id>/`
  - Supports explicit metadata for `category`, `genre`, `project`, and `run-id`
  - Infers sane defaults when labels are omitted
  - Restricts generated file writes to the declared workspace root

- **Run manifests and indexes**
  - Writes a per-run `PLAYGROUND_MANIFEST.json` with task/source metadata, hats used, summary, status, and generated files
  - Generates workspace indexes for easier browsing:
    - root `PLAYGROUND_INDEX.md`
    - per-category `CATEGORY_INDEX.md`

- **Workflow and CLI plumbing**
  - Extends `hats-task.yml` to accept playground metadata and pass source repo / PR / issue context into task runs
  - Uploads both the task output artifact and the full playground artifact
  - Extends `scripts/hat` with:
    - `--category`
    - `--genre`
    - `--project`

- **Model fallback behavior**
  - Task mode now retries comparable configured models if the selected Ollama model fails
  - Preserves the configured primary/fallback preference, then expands to other comparable models from the model config
  - Records fallback usage in task notes when a non-primary model succeeds

- **Docs**
  - Updates task-mode examples and docs to describe the playground layout, artifact behavior, and fallback semantics

Example:

```bash
hat task generate_code "Build a FastAPI auth module with JWT" \
  --repo myorg/app \
  --pr 42 \
  --category code \
  --genre api \
  --project auth-service
```

This produces a structured run directory like:

```text
/tmp/hats-playground/code/api/auth-service/run-<id>/
```

body:
The `bio-digital-ci-cd.yml` workflow references `src/signal_processing/audit_spike_sorting.py` in the "Spike Detection Quality Audit" step, but the file never existed — causing every CI run to fail with `[Errno 2] No such file or directory`.

## Changes

- **New script: `src/signal_processing/audit_spike_sorting.py`**
  - Generates synthetic extracellular traces with ground-truth spike positions injected into Gaussian noise
  - Runs a threshold-based detector mirroring the SSD logic in `template_matching.rs`
  - Matches detections to ground-truth spikes within a ±30 frame (±1 ms @ 30 kHz) tolerance window
  - Asserts false-negative and false-positive rates stay ≤ 10%; exits non-zero on failure so CI fails loudly on regressions
  - Covers 4 benchmark scenarios: single spike (low/high noise), multiple spikes, and dense spike trains

```python
# Example benchmark entry
("Dense spikes — medium noise",
 list(range(BENCHMARK_SPIKE_INTERVAL_FRAMES, BENCHMARK_DURATION_FRAMES, BENCHMARK_SPIKE_INTERVAL_FRAMES)),
 BENCHMARK_DURATION_FRAMES, 0.10, 0.9)
```

Follows the same structure and exit-code contract as the existing `verify_latency.py` audit script.

author: rubencerna2079
body:
## Why make this change?
- Closes issue #3258
Whenever we use the `dab start` command the CLI overrides the minimum LogLevel from the configuration file. This is acceptable only if we use the `--LogLevel` flag. If we do not use that flag, the LogLevel for each namespace should be decided by the configuration file.

## What is this change?
This change moves the `args.Add` methods inside the `ConfigGenerator.cs` so that they are only applied when we use the `--LogLevel` flag. Having these arguments causes DAB to not allow any changes to the LogLevel in the loggers, since those arguments were always being added, DAB always assumed the CLI was overriding the LogLevel when it was not expected as it would use the `--LogLevel` flag to determine if it was an `IsLogLevelOverridenByCli` scenario.

## How was this tested?

- [ ] Integration Tests
- [x] Unit Tests
- [x] Manual Tests
Tested with different configurations of the namespaces in the `log-level` property inside the config file.
Note: ALL these manual tests were tested by running the CLI as well as running DAB through Visual Studio.
Config file includes:
```
"log-level": {
    "Azure.DataApiBuilder.Core.Services.ISqlMetadataProvider": "Information",
    "Azure.DataApiBuilder.Core": "Debug",
    "Azure.DataApiBuilder.Config.FileSystemRuntimeConfigLoader": "Error",
    "default": "Warning"
}
```
Expected results:
- All the logs from `Azure.DataApiBuilder.Core.Services.ISqlMetadataProvider` will provide logs from log level information and above.
- All logs from `Azure.DataApiBuilder.Core` and its sub-namespaces that are not from `ISqlMetadataProvider` will provide logs from log level debug and above.
- All logs from `Azure.DataApiBuilder.Config.FileSystemRuntimeConfigLoader` will provide logs from log level error and above.
- Everything else will provide logs from log level warning and above, including CLI.

Config file includes:
```
"log-level": {
    "Azure.DataApiBuilder.Core": "Information",
    "Azure.DataApiBuilder.Config": "Debug",
}
```
Expected results:
- All logs from `Azure.DataApiBuilder.Core` and its sub-namespaces will provide logs from log level information and above.
- All logs from `Azure.DataApiBuilder.Config` and its sub-namespaces will provide logs from log level debug and above.
- Everything else will provide logs from log level debug and above with `host.mode = development`, including CLI.

Config file includes:
```
"log-level": {
    "Default: none
}
```
Expected results:
- No logs will be printed, including CLI.

## Sample Request(s)
dab start --LogLevel information

dab start (With config file default value debug)

body:
### Motivation
- Introduce two chip-style resynthesis effects to produce single-note "chiptune" textures from samples and expose them to the UI. 
- Improve effect UI ergonomics by separating envelope/utility (fade/reverse/reset) controls and prevent clipping of buttons. 
- Make effect application selection-aware and robust to length changes by preserving and scaling loop points when effects change audio length. 
- Provide cursor state callbacks so long-running audio operations can update the UI cursor state.

### Description
- Added two new effects to `AudioEffectsProcessor`: `ApplyChipifyMonoEffect` and `ApplyChipifyDeluxeEffect`, plus an internal `ChipWaveType` enum and helpers (`EstimateFundamentalFrequency`, `EstimateRms`, `EstimateZeroCrossingRate`, `QuantizeFrequencyToSemitone`, `BuildAnalysisSignal`, `ApplySampleAndHold`, `GenerateChipSample`, `BytesToFloats`, etc.) to perform pitch-tracking, envelope estimation and chip-wave resynthesis. 
- Integrated the new effects into processing flows by registering `chipify_mono` and `chipify_deluxe` in `ApplyAllModifications` and adding tracked handlers `ApplyChipifyMonoEffect` and `ApplyChipifyDeluxeEffect` that use the selection-aware effect callback model. 
- Reworked the effects UI in `InitializeEffectsPanel`: resized the main effects panel, added a new `fadePanel` for envelope/utility buttons (Fade In/Out, Reverse, Reset), and added `Chipify Mono` and `Chipify Deluxe` buttons wired to the new handlers. 
- Improved tracked-effect application via `ApplyTrackedEffect` to call a provided callback `effectFunction()` (so selection-aware effects honor loop selections) and to scale/restores loop points when audio length changes after an effect; added cursor callback wiring so `AudioEffectsProcessor` uses `SetBusyCursor`/`SetNormalCursor`. 
- Updated `README.md` features list to include `Chipify Mono effect` and `Chipify Deluxe effect`.

### Testing

Greetings. Renovate would like you to know that there's an update available for your consideration.

This PR contains the following updates:

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>actions/github-script (actions/github-script)</summary>

### [`v9.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/actions/github-script/releases/tag/v9.0.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/actions/github-script/compare/v8.0.0...v9.0.0)

**New features:**

- **`getOctokit` factory function** — Available directly in the script context. Create additional authenticated Octokit clients with different tokens for multi-token workflows, GitHub App tokens, and cross-org access. See [Creating additional clients with `getOctokit`](https://redirect.github.com/actions/github-script#creating-additional-clients-with-getoctokit) for details and examples.
- **Orchestration ID in user-agent** — The `ACTIONS_ORCHESTRATION_ID` environment variable is automatically appended to the user-agent string for request tracing.

**Breaking changes:**

- **`require('@​actions/github')` no longer works in scripts.** The upgrade to `@actions/github` v9 (ESM-only) means `require('@​actions/github')` will fail at runtime. If you previously used patterns like `const { getOctokit } = require('@​actions/github')` to create secondary clients, use the new injected `getOctokit` function instead — it's available directly in the script context with no imports needed.
- `getOctokit` is now an injected function parameter. Scripts that declare `const getOctokit = ...` or `let getOctokit = ...` will get a `SyntaxError` because JavaScript does not allow `const`/`let` redeclaration of function parameters. Use the injected `getOctokit` directly, or use `var getOctokit = ...` if you need to redeclare it.
- If your script accesses other `@actions/github` internals beyond the standard `github`/`octokit` client, you may need to update those references for v9 compatibility.

author: dqian
body:
## Summary

First game migration to the new casino-server backend. Roulette spins now go through `POST /games/roulette/rounds` when the user is signed in and in play money mode — the server runs the RNG, debits the stake, settles the round through the new `AccountService` + ledger, and returns the authoritative `balanceAfter`. The CLI uses the server's winning number as the animation target instead of computing locally.

Pairs with casino-server PR #1 (must be deployed first).

## What changed

- **`auth/client.ts`** — new typed wrapper `playRouletteRound(token, account, bets)` that posts to the new endpoint. Bet amounts go over the wire as integer-cents strings to preserve precision.
- **`roulette/game.ts`** — `spin()` branches on `loggedIn && play money`:
  - **Server path**: posts the round, awaits the result, then animates toward the server's `winningNumber`. On HTTP error or network failure: refund local stakes, return to betting phase, show error.
  - **Local path**: unchanged `Math.random` flow for offline/unauth/non-play modes.
- **`finishSpin()`** — checks for stashed `serverBalanceAfter`. If present, uses the server's winnings + balance directly. Otherwise computes locally (existing behavior).
- **`types.ts`** — adds `serverWinnings` and `serverBalanceAfter` to `RouletteState` for the spin → finishSpin handoff. Reset to `null` on `newRound()`.
- **`tui.ts`** — skips `syncBalanceToServer` while on the roulette screen. The server is already authoritative there; local debits during bet placement are ephemeral until the round is submitted.

## Behavior matrix

| state                          | spin path  | balance source         |
| ------------------------------ | ---------- | ---------------------- |
| signed in, play money          | server     | server `balanceAfter`  |
| signed in, real money          | n/a        | (menu disables)        |
| signed out                     | local      | local `Math.random`    |
| signed in, server unreachable  | server fails → bets refunded, error shown |

## Real money path

Intentionally not enabled in this PR. Once play money is verified working in production, enabling real money is a one-line change in `casino-server/src/games/roulette/routes.ts` (remove the `503` guard) plus removing the `disabledByRealMode` check on the roulette menu item. The CLI code path is already wired for `account: "real"` — the `useServer` gate currently restricts to `play` only because real money roulette is server-side disabled.

## Test plan

- [ ] Pull casino-server PR #1, run migrations, restart server
- [ ] Sign in to the cli with a real account
- [ ] In play money mode, place bets and spin — verify the wheel lands on the server's number
- [ ] Verify the post-round balance matches a server `/me` query
- [ ] Test winning round (bet on a color, hit it) → balance increases by exactly the payout
- [ ] Test losing round → balance decreases by exactly the stake
- [ ] Multi-bet round (e.g. red + black + zero) → only winning bets pay
- [ ] Place bets, hit Escape → bets refunded locally
- [ ] Sign out, play roulette → falls back to local RNG (offline mode)
- [ ] Sign in, kill the server, place bets, spin → see "Could not reach server" + bets refunded
- [ ] Switch to real money mode → roulette still shows "Coming Soon" in the menu
- [ ] After several rounds, verify casino-server `ledger_entries` has matching `stake`/`payout` rows

## Notes

- Network latency adds a small delay between hitting Enter and the wheel starting to spin. Acceptable; user sees the "Spinning..." state briefly while the request flies. Could mitigate later by starting the animation optimistically and updating the target when the response arrives, but adds complexity for marginal benefit.
- Real money flip will be a tiny follow-up PR once play money is confirmed working.

author: copilot
body:
This change adds the issue-level design for the destination browsing experience: a light, image-first `/destinations` list page with URL-driven search/filter interactions, plus an immersive `/destinations/[id]` detail page. The design aligns the new UI work with the existing requirements, shared visual system, and already-implemented destination query APIs.

- **Scope captured**
  - Defines the destination list and detail page goals, non-goals, and current repo state
  - Anchors the work to `docs/requirements.md` and `docs/design.md`
  - Explicitly treats destination browsing as the default public entry flow

- **Proposed page architecture**
  - Specifies `travel-website/src/app/destinations/page.tsx` for the list page
  - Specifies `travel-website/src/app/destinations/[id]/page.tsx` for the detail page
  - Recommends redirecting `/` to `/destinations`
  - Includes a route-segment loading state for smoother transitions

- **Data and interaction model**
  - Recommends server-rendered pages calling the destination service directly
  - Proposes shared query-param normalization so page behavior and API validation stay aligned
  - Defines URL-driven search, filters, sorting, reset behavior, and pagination semantics

- **UI composition**
  - Introduces a `DestinationCard` component for image-led cards with soft hover lift
  - Introduces a `DestinationFilters` client component for query-string updates
  - Defines detail-page sections for hero imagery, descriptive content, and structured metadata

- **Design constraints**
  - Reuses the existing light/airy token system and glass treatment
  - Emphasizes whitespace, rounded surfaces, soft shadows, and restrained teal accents
  - Calls out accessibility requirements for labels, headings, alt text, and metadata readability

- **Implementation guidance**
  - Breaks the work into a minimal, ordered implementation plan
  - Adds focused test recommendations for cards, filters, and shared query parsing

Example structure from the design:

```ts
// destination browse flow
"/" -> redirect("/destinations")

/destinations
  -> parse searchParams
  -> normalize query state
  -> listDestinations(...)

/destinations/[id]
  -> validate id
  -> getDestinationById(id)
  -> render image-led detail layout
```

### Motivation
- Make server-side XLSX→PDF conversion more robust across Unix and Windows deployments and safer to invoke.
- Provide a reliable client-side export path when the `autoTable` plugin is unavailable in `jsPDF`.

### Description
- Update `convert-xlsx-to-pdf.php` to try multiple `soffice`/`libreoffice` binary locations (including common Windows paths), use `escapeshellarg` for safer argument quoting, and add `--nologo --nodefault` flags to the conversion command.
- Add a check in `exportRowsAsPdf` so it uses `doc.autoTable` when available and returns immediately after saving, and otherwise falls back to a simple, paginated plain-text table renderer that clips long lines and paginates manually.
- Keep existing behavior of saving the generated PDF via `doc.save(fileName)` for both code paths.

### Testing
- Ran the repository's automated test suite and it completed successfully.
- Performed a CI smoke test for the conversion endpoint by POSTing a minimal XLSX to `convert-xlsx-to-pdf.php` and confirming a PDF is produced when a LibreOffice binary is available.
- Executed frontend unit tests that exercise `exportRowsAsPdf` and its fallback path, and they passed.

author: 0x-squidsol
body:
## Summary
- `process_withdraw` had **zero validation** on `user_ata` (collateral destination, account[5])
- `process_deposit` (lines 480-504) and `process_deposit_junior` (lines 1856-1877) both validate user_ata's mint and owner — `process_withdraw` was the only handler that skipped this
- An attacker can pass `vault.key` as `user_ata`, causing an SPL Token self-transfer (vault→vault, no-op on balance) while LP tokens are still burned and `total_withdrawn` is incremented
- This desyncs pool accounting from actual vault balance (`vault_balance > total_pool_value()`)

## Attack Impact
- Pool accounting undervalues actual vault holdings
- Subsequent depositors get more LP per collateral than they should (LP pricing based on deflated pool_value)
- HWM floor calculations use the wrong TVL
- Deposit cap checks use the wrong pool value
- The attacker sacrifices their own LP (self-griefing), but could profit if they hold positions via other accounts

## Fix
Added before any CPI calls (after line 727, before vault_auth PDA derivation):

1. **Vault aliasing check:** `user_ata.key != vault.key` — blocks the self-transfer attack vector
2. **Mint check:** `user_ata` mint must match `pool.collateral_mint` — defense-in-depth, fail-fast with clear error

**Owner check deliberately omitted** — on withdrawal, the user burns their own LP and should be free to direct collateral to any address (cold wallet, multisig, etc.). This differs from `process_deposit` where the owner check prevents a delegation attack that drains a victim's ATA.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo build` — compiles cleanly
- [x] `cargo clippy` — zero warnings
- [x] 3 independent agents confirmed the bug and agreed on the fix approach

body:
**Is this PR adding new feature or fix a BUG?**

Fix BUG (security vulnerabilities).

**Is this pull request related to any issue? If yes, please link the issue.**

No linked issue — this came from a security audit of the codebase.

---

## Summary

Fixes five security issues found during a codebase audit:

1. **Timing-attack-vulnerable API key comparison** (`tools/api_server.py`): Replaced `!=` with `hmac.compare_digest()` to prevent timing side-channel attacks on the bearer token check.

2. **Overly permissive CORS** (`tools/api_server.py`): `CORSConfig()` with no arguments defaulted to allowing **all origins** (`re.compile(".*")`). Now requires explicit `--allowed-origins` flag; CORS is disabled by default.

3. **Path traversal via `reference_id`** (`fish_speech/inference_engine/reference_loader.py`): User-supplied `reference_id` was used directly in `Path("references") / id` with no sanitization. Added `_validate_reference_id()` to reject path separators, dot-prefixed names, and resolved paths that escape the `references/` directory.

4. **Internal exception details leaked to clients** (`tools/server/exception_handler.py`): The generic exception handler returned `str(exc)` to clients, potentially exposing file paths, library internals, etc. Now returns a static `"Internal server error"` message (full traceback is still logged server-side).

5. **Hardcoded placeholder API key in client** (`tools/api_client.py`): Replaced `default="YOUR_API_KEY"` with `os.environ.get("FISH_SPEECH_API_KEY")`.

## ⚠️ Reviewer Checklist

- [ ] **Breaking change — CORS default**: Previously all origins were allowed; now CORS is off by default. Any deployment relying on cross-origin access without `--allowed-origins` will break. Is this acceptable, or should there be a migration/deprecation warning?
- [ ] **Path traversal validation**: `_validate_reference_id` rejects IDs starting with `.` — confirm no legitimate reference IDs use dot-prefixed names.
- [ ] **No tests added** for the new `_validate_reference_id` logic or the CORS/auth changes.

author: jonhill90
body:
## Summary
The browser tool (Playwright) was broken across multiple tool calls because `asyncio.run()` creates and destroys a new event loop per call, killing the browser page between calls.

**Before**: Each `asyncio.run(execute_tool_call(...))` in `_run_tool_loop` created a fresh event loop. When the browser tool launched Playwright, it bound to that loop. When the next tool call used `asyncio.run()` again, the previous loop was destroyed, killing the browser page. The `_browser_page` global pointed to a dead object.

**After**: A persistent event loop runs in a dedicated daemon thread (`tool-event-loop`). All async tool calls are dispatched to it via `asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe()`. The browser page survives across tool calls, and cached screenshots remain valid for the `/screenshot` endpoint.

## Changes
- `services/agentbox/app/chat.py`:
  - Added `_get_tool_loop()` — creates a persistent `asyncio.AbstractEventLoop` in a daemon thread
  - Added `_run_async(coro)` — dispatches coroutines to the persistent loop via `run_coroutine_threadsafe`
  - Replaced `asyncio.run(execute_tool_call(...))` with `_run_async(execute_tool_call(...))`

## How screenshot caching works (already in place)

author: iceman12276
body:
## Who

- Isaac Quintero
- Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context)

## What

- Delete orphaned `sdk/package-lock.json` (2068 lines, dead code)
- Add `"name": "pqdb"` to root `package.json` so `npm install` produces a deterministic lockfile regardless of which directory it runs from

## When

2026-04-09 (America/New_York)

## Where

- `sdk/package-lock.json` — deleted in full
- `package.json` — single line added (`"name": "pqdb"`)
- `package-lock.json` (root) — byte-for-byte unchanged from main

## Why

Semgrep SCA flagged 4 supply-chain findings against `sdk/package-lock.json`, including 2 HIGH/HIGH vite vulnerabilities:

| Severity | Confidence | Package | CWE | Vuln |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HIGH | HIGH | vite (7.3.1) | CWE-284 | `server.fs.deny` bypass via `?raw` / `?import&raw` query — exposes `.env`, certs, sensitive files |
| HIGH | HIGH | vite (7.3.1) | CWE-306 | Vite Dev Server WebSocket exposes `fetchModule`, unauthenticated arbitrary file read |
| MEDIUM | LOW | vite (7.3.1) | CWE-22 | Path traversal variant |
| MEDIUM | LOW | picomatch (4.0.x) | CWE-1321 | Prototype pollution |

Investigation showed `sdk/package-lock.json` is an **orphan** from before this repo became an npm workspace. The active source of truth is the root `package-lock.json`, which is what `npm install` actually uses (workspaces: `sdk`, `mcp` per root `package.json`). The root lockfile pulls vite **6.4.2** via vitest — not in the affected version range, no findings against it.

The orphan was sitting in git tracking vite 7.3.1 with known CVEs, getting scanned by Semgrep, and producing real findings against dead code. Anyone running the dashboard locally with `--host 0.0.0.0` (per `CLAUDE.md`) would have been on a vulnerable dev server config IF the code had actually been using vite 7.3.1 — but it isn't. The advisories are real, the file is dead.

## How

**Considered:**
- **Bump vite in the orphan to a patched version**: rejected, would preserve the structural mistake (two competing lockfiles for the same workspace) and Semgrep would just keep flagging the next CVE.
- **Add npm `overrides` at the root to force a vite version**: rejected, unnecessary because the active root lockfile already pins vite 6.4.2 which is not in the affected range.
- **Delete the orphan (chosen)**: kills 4 of 7 SCA findings outright (3 vite + 1 picomatch) and removes the structural source of confusion. The active workspace lockfile is unchanged. Smallest possible diff for the largest possible reduction in attack surface.

**The `"name": "pqdb"` package.json addition** is a separate-but-related fix: `npm install` was using the directory name as the lockfile project name when no `name` field existed, causing every worktree to flip-flop the lockfile (e.g., `worktree-vite-bump` instead of `pqdb`). Pinning the name makes the lockfile deterministic regardless of where the command runs.

**Trade-offs:**
- Anyone still running `cd sdk && npm install` (instead of the workspace `npm install` at root) will fail to find the orphan lockfile — but they shouldn't be doing that since the repo became a workspace. The workspace pattern is documented in `CLAUDE.md`.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm install` at root succeeds, regenerates workspace lockfile with vite 6.4.2 unchanged (byte-identical to main)
- [x] `npm test --workspace=sdk` — 238/238 pass
- [x] `npm run build --workspace=sdk` — ESM + CJS + DTS build success
- [x] `npm run typecheck --workspace=sdk` — clean
- [x] `npm audit` reports 0 vulnerabilities
- [ ] CI on this PR — all 5 jobs (SDK, Backend, Sec Gate, E2E, Dashboard E2E) green
- [ ] Semgrep Cloud Platform scan on this PR confirms 4 findings drop off (3 vite + 1 picomatch in sdk/package-lock.json)

## Non-goals

- **3 remaining h3 findings in `dashboard/package-lock.json`** — independent of vite/picomatch, require a TanStack Start / h3 upgrade. All MEDIUM/LOW or LOW/LOW severity. Tracked as a Phase 5d follow-up in the prd.json.
- **Bumping vite to 7.x or 8.x** — not needed; current 6.4.2 is unaffected.
- **Restructuring sdk to be standalone again** — workspaces are the right pattern, the orphan is the bug.

author: madmax983
body:
**What:**
Optimized the `fill_circle` function in `crates/abrash-render/src/rasterizer/circle.rs` to completely eliminate Bresenham scanline overdraw.

**Why:**
The previous algorithm naively drew horizontal scanlines (`draw_horizontal_line_unchecked`) on every single `x` increment within the inner loop. Because `y` decrements much slower than `x` increments (especially near the poles), this caused the exact same row to be written to the framebuffer multiple times per frame, heavily wasting memory bandwidth and CPU cycles.

**Impact:**
Massive performance improvement in solid circle rendering. By tracking the `last_y` boundary and only issuing a horizontal draw call when the vertical scanline actually changes, we guarantee 0% overdraw.

**Measurement:**
`cargo bench --bench circle_bench` (r=100)
- Before: ~6.20 µs
- After: ~1.31 µs
- Improvement: ~79% faster.

author: copilot
body:
`wave` is a browser game deploying to Azure Static Web Apps — it has no reason to publish to npm. `semantic-release` was including `@semantic-release/npm` by default, causing `verifyConditions` to fail on missing/invalid `NPM_TOKEN`.

## Changes

- **`release.config.mjs`** (new) — explicitly configures `semantic-release` to use only `commit-analyzer`, `release-notes-generator`, and `github` plugins; npm plugin excluded
- **`.github/workflows/ci-cd.yml`** — strips all npm auth from the `release` job:
  - Removes `Set up npm auth` step
  - Removes `registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org'` from Node.js setup
  - Removes `NPM_TOKEN` / `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` from `Semantic Release` env; only `GITHUB_TOKEN` remains
- **`package.json`** — adds `"private": true` to prevent accidental future publishes

```js
// release.config.mjs
export default {
  branches: ["main"],
  plugins: [
    "@semantic-release/commit-analyzer",
    "@semantic-release/release-notes-generator",
    "@semantic-release/github",
  ],
};
```

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>


## Problem

The CI/CD pipeline is failing because `semantic-release` is trying to publish the `wave` package to npm, but this is a browser-based game that deploys to Azure Static Web Apps — it should never be published to npm. The `NPM_TOKEN` secret is missing/invalid, causing the `verifyConditions` step to fail.

## Solution

1. **Add a `release.config.mjs`** file at the repo root that disables the `@semantic-release/npm` plugin and only uses the GitHub plugin:

```javascript
export default {
  branches: ["main"],
  plugins: [
    "@semantic-release/commit-analyzer",
    "@semantic-release/release-notes-generator",
    "@semantic-release/github",
  ],
};
```

2. **Update `.github/workflows/ci-cd.yml`** — in the `release` job, remove all npm token-related steps and env vars:
   - Remove the `"Set up npm auth"` step (`echo "//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=..." > ~/.npmrc`)
   - Remove `registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org'` from the `Setup Node.js` step
   - Remove `NPM_TOKEN` and `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` from the `Semantic Release` step's `env` block
   - Keep only `GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` in the env

The `Semantic Release` step's run script (the bash block that captures before/after tags) should remain unchanged.

Also add `"private": true` to `package.json` to make it explicit this package is not meant to be published to npm.


The following is the prior conversation context from the user's chat exploration (may be truncated):

User: The build is failing due to **two main issues**:

---

### ❌ Issue 1: Invalid/Missing npm Token (Root Cause)

```
npm error code E401
npm error 401 Unauthorized - GET https://registry.npmjs.org/-/whoami
SemanticReleaseError: Invalid npm token.
```

`semantic-release` is trying to publish to npm but is failing because it cannot authenticate with the npm registry. The `NPM_TOKEN` secret is either missing, expired, or invalid.

**Fix:**
1. Go to [npmjs.com](https://www.npmjs.com) and generate a new **Automation token** (or Granular Access Token with publish permissions).
2. Add or update the secret in your repo:
   - Navigate to **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions**
   - Add/update the secret named `NPM_TOKEN` with the new token value.
3. Ensure your workflow references it correctly, e.g.:
   ```yaml
   env:
     NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
   ```

---

### ❌ Issue 2: OIDC Token Exchange Failed

```
OIDC token exchange with the npm registry failed: 404 OIDC token exchange error - package not found
```

If you're using npm's **provenance/OIDC publishing**, the package may not yet exist on npm or the package name doesn't match. Either:
- Publish the package manually once first to register it on npm, **or**
- Disable OIDC provenance if it's not needed by setting `"npmPublishProvenance": false` in your `semantic-release` config.

---

### ❌ Issue 3: GitHub Label Validation Error (Secondary)

Validation Failed: {"value":"semantic-release","resource":"Label","field":"name","code":"invalid"}

This is a **secondary failure** — `semantic-release` tried to create a GitHub issue to notify about the failure but couldn't create/find the `semantic-release` label. This is a side effect of Issue 1 and will likely resolve itself once the npm token is fixed.

---

### Summary of Steps to Fix

|------|--------|
| 1 | Generate a new npm token at npmjs.com |
| 2 | Add `NPM_TOKEN` to your repo's Actions secrets |
| 3 | Verify your workflow sets the `NPM_TOKEN` env variable |

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
**Is this PR adding new feature or fix a BUG?**

Fix BUG — addresses multiple security vulnerabilities found during a codebase audit.

**Is this pull request related to any issue? If yes, please link the issue.**

No existing issue.

---

### Changes

**1. CORS restricted to localhost by default** (`tools/api_server.py`)
`CORSConfig()` was passed empty, which results in a permissive wildcard CORS policy. Now explicitly restricts `allow_origins` to localhost, with allowed methods and headers scoped down. Configurable at runtime via the `FISH_CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS` environment variable (comma-separated origins).

**2. Auth middleware actually wired into routes** (`tools/api_server.py`)
The `api_auth` middleware was defined but never applied — `self.routes = routes` bypassed it entirely. Now uses `Routes(routes, http_middlewares=[api_auth])` so the `--api-key` flag actually enforces authentication.

**3. Internal error details no longer leaked to clients** (`tools/server/exception_handler.py`)
`str(exc)` was returned directly in the JSON response body for unhandled exceptions, potentially exposing file paths, library internals, etc. Now returns a generic message; the full traceback is still logged server-side.

**4. Placeholder API key removed from client** (`tools/api_client.py`)
Default changed from `"YOUR_API_KEY"` to `None`. The `Authorization` header is now only sent when a key is explicitly provided.

**5. Input validation on `ServeChatRequest`** (`fish_speech/utils/schema.py`)
Added Pydantic `Field` bounds to `max_new_tokens` (1–4096), `top_p`, `temperature`, `repetition_penalty`, and `num_samples` (1–16) to prevent resource-exhaustion via unbounded values.

---

### Review checklist
- [ ] **CORS default origins don't include ports** — the default `http://localhost,http://127.0.0.1` won't match `http://localhost:7860` (Gradio) or `http://localhost:8080`. Verify whether port-qualified origins should be included, or whether same-origin requests make this a non-issue for the typical deployment.
- [ ] **`max_new_tokens` cap of 4096 and `num_samples` cap of 16** — confirm these upper bounds are appropriate and won't break existing legitimate usage.
- [ ] **`Routes(routes, http_middlewares=[api_auth])`** — verify this is the correct kui API for applying middleware to all routes.

body: ## Summary Implements a large slice of Git’s `fetch --recurse-submodules` behavior: recording ref tips across fetches, walking newly fetched history for gitlink changes, spawning nested `grit fetch` with the right flags, fixing nested submodule path resolution for multi-segment `.gitmodules` entries, and correcting `From …` display URLs when the current repo’s git dir lives under `.git/modules/`. ## Test status `t5526-fetch-submodules.sh` is **not** fully passing yet (harness last run: **16/56**). This commit is incremental scaffolding toward full parity. ## Key changes - `grit-lib`: new `fetch_submodules` module (rev-list–based changed gitlink collection, recurse parsing helpers). - `grit fetch`: `--dry-run`, `--no-write-fetch-head`, hidden `--recurse-submodules-default` / `--submodule-prefix`; records submodule-related OIDs; merges tips for `fetch --all`; skips submodule recursion in `--porcelain` mode (Git compatibility). - `resolve_submodule_chain`: match longest `.gitmodules` path prefix so nested paths like `subdir/deepsubmodule` resolve. - `configured_remote_base`: strip `/.git/modules/...` so relative file URLs match upstream tests.

body:
This updates the Specrail MCP workflow surface from a passive payload viewer to an interactive MCP App. Hosts can now render workflow state, feature/outcome overview, test readiness, delegation prompts, and guided control actions from a single `ui://specrail/workflow` app.

- **MCP App contract**
  - Upgrades `ui://specrail/workflow` to an MCP Apps resource with `text/html;profile=mcp-app`
  - Advertises `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui` server capability
  - Adds UI resource metadata so hosts can treat the workflow panel as a first-class app surface

- **Workflow app UI**
  - Replaces the placeholder JSON panel with a control center for:
    - current workflow status and blockers
    - feature/outcome overview board
    - outcome test review details
    - delegation payloads
    - quick workflow controls for refresh, resume, activate, implement, verify, and advance
  - Preserves delegated prompts in-app instead of dropping them on refresh

- **Tool integration**
  - Attaches `_meta.ui.resourceUri` to the key workflow tools so hosts can render results into the workflow app consistently
  - Uses existing structured workflow actions and overview payloads as the control model rather than introducing a parallel UI-only state machine

- **Bridge hardening**
  - Adds MCP app handshake/display-mode support
  - Reports dynamic size to the host
  - Tightens message handling around trusted parent/host origin tracking for iframe bridge traffic

- **Docs and contract coverage**
  - Updates MCP server coverage to assert the new app MIME type, extension capability, and tool UI metadata
  - Refreshes plugin docs to describe the workflow app as an interactive MCP surface

Example of the updated MCP app wiring:

```json
{
  "name": "specrail_status",
  "_meta": {
    "ui": {
      "resourceUri": "ui://specrail/workflow",
      "visibility": ["model", "app"]
    }
  }
}
```

author: ahsanhabib9191
body:
🚨 **Severity:** CRITICAL

💡 **Vulnerability:** Several endpoints in the Sheet and Research API layers (`get_my_chats`, `create_conversation`, and `create_research_queue`) were missing authentication checks. Furthermore, lookup operations utilized `findById` without validating the user's ownership of the record, creating an Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) vulnerability. In `create_conversation`, new sessions were hardcoded to be created under a `'temp-user'` rather than the logged-in user.

🎯 **Impact:** An attacker could bypass authentication to fetch all sessions from the database (`get_my_chats`) or interact with any chat or conversation created by another user by guessing or enumerating their database IDs (`create_research_queue`, `create_conversation`). This leads to severe data exposure and the potential for unauthorized data manipulation.

🔧 **Fix:** 
- Enforced authentication checks using the `getAuthenticatedUser()` utility on all three endpoints.
- Replaced the vulnerable `findById` queries with secure `findOne({ _id: chatId, userId: user._id || user.id })` queries, ensuring proper ownership authorization.
- Modified the creation flow in `create_conversation` to assign the authenticated user's ID to new sessions instead of the hardcoded `'temp-user'`.
- Failed securely by returning standard `401 Unauthorized` and `404 Not Found` errors.

✅ **Verification:**
- Verified code changes locally to confirm correct implementation of the auth checks and scoped queries.
- Ran `pnpm lint` (failed expectedly due to pre-existing config issues) and the project test suite (`vitest run`). Verified that tests for related components and routes continue to pass successfully.

author: manjunathgujjar
body:
## Summary
Fixes #7441

`ensure_config` assigned `metadata` (and other `COPIABLE_KEYS`) by reference instead of copying them. When configurable values like `thread_id` were later written into `_empty_metadata`, they mutated the caller's original config dict. Subsequent invocations would then see stale configurable values injected into their metadata.

## Root Cause

In the loop over user-provided configs, `configurable` (CONF) was correctly copied with `.copy()`, but `metadata` and other `COPIABLE_KEYS` were assigned by reference:

```python
# Before — metadata assigned by reference, gets mutated later
if k == CONF:
    empty[k] = cast(dict, v).copy()
else:
    empty[k] = v

# After — all COPIABLE_KEYS are copied consistently
if k in COPIABLE_KEYS:
    empty[k] = v.copy()
else:
    empty[k] = v
```

The subsequent block writes configurable keys into `_empty_metadata`, which was the same object as the caller's original `metadata` dict. After the fix each call gets its own copy.

## Changes
- `libs/langgraph/langgraph/_internal/_config.py`: Check `k in COPIABLE_KEYS` instead of `k == CONF`, consistent with how `var_child_runnable_config` is already handled in the same function.
- `libs/langgraph/tests/test_config_async.py`: Two tests covering single and multiple invocations.

## How to Test
```bash
pytest libs/langgraph/tests/test_config_async.py::test_ensure_config_does_not_mutate_shared_metadata -v
pytest libs/langgraph/tests/test_config_async.py::test_ensure_config_does_not_mutate_shared_metadata_multiple_invocations -v
```

author: octo-patch
body:
Fixes #2613

## Problem

`SkillsMiddleware` cached `skills_metadata` in agent state after the first turn and skipped reloading on subsequent turns:

```python
# Skip if skills_metadata is already present in state (even if empty)
if "skills_metadata" in state:
    return None
```

This meant that skills created during a session (e.g., via `write_file`) were never discovered in the same session — users had to restart entirely.

## Solution

Remove the early-return cache check so skills are reloaded from backend sources on every agent turn. This ensures dynamically created or updated skills are available in the next turn without a session restart.

## Testing

- Updated `test_before_agent_skips_loading_if_metadata_present` → `test_before_agent_always_reloads_skills` to verify that skills are reloaded even when `skills_metadata` is already present in state.
- Updated the async counterpart `test_abefore_agent_skips_loading_if_metadata_present` → `test_abefore_agent_always_reloads_skills` with the same logic.
- All existing tests continue to pass.

author: slawomirbabicz
body:
## Pin GitHub Actions to commit SHAs

GitHub Actions referenced by tag (e.g. `actions/checkout@v4`) use a mutable pointer — the tag owner can move it to a different commit at any time, including a malicious one. This is the attack vector used in the tj-actions/changed-files incident (CVE-2025-30066).

Pinning to a full 40-character commit SHA makes the reference immutable. The `# tag` comment preserves human readability so reviewers can tell which version is pinned.

Important: a SHA can also originate from a forked repository. A malicious actor can fork an action, push a compromised commit to the fork, and the SHA will resolve — but it won't exist in the upstream canonical repo. Each SHA in this PR was verified against the action's canonical repository (not a fork).

### Changes

- `actions/checkout@v4` -> `actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5 # v4.3.1`

author: henrik-me
body:
## Problem
The prod-deploy workflow's image verification step returned HTTP 401 when checking GHCR.

**Root cause:** GHCR uses Docker Registry V2 auth which requires a token exchange flow. Direct basic auth with \GITHUB_TOKEN\ doesn't work — only PATs support direct basic auth against GHCR endpoints.

## Fix
Implement the proper Docker Registry V2 token exchange:
1. Authenticate with GHCR token service (\/token\) using basic auth + \GITHUB_TOKEN\
2. Receive a scoped bearer token for \epository:pull\  
3. Use the bearer token to query the manifests API

This follows the same auth pattern that \docker login\ / \docker/login-action\ uses internally.

## Testing
- Workflow change only — no application code affected
- Will be validated by the next \prod-deploy.yml\ run

author: copilot
body:
No fast (offline) tests existed for the `Phi3MoELongRoPEModel` builder (`PhiMoEForCausalLM` architecture). This adds a fully offline test suite covering ONNX graph construction and CUDA inference.

## Changes

- **`tests/fast/test_random_phimoe.py`** – new test file with:
  - `_make_phimoe_config()` – tiny `Phi3Config` patched to satisfy `Phi3MoELongRoPEModel` requirements: `architectures=["PhiMoEForCausalLM"]`, `max_pos ≠ original_max_pos` (LongRoPE dispatch), `rope_scaling` with `short_factor`/`long_factor` (length = `head_size // 2`), and `num_local_experts`/`num_experts_per_tok`.
  - `_make_phimoe_torch_model()` – minimal PyTorch model with the exact attribute structure the builder accesses: `layer.block_sparse_moe.{gate, experts[i].{w1,w2,w3}}`, `nn.LayerNorm` (not RMSNorm — required because `simple=False` means the builder reads both `.weight` and `.bias`), layer class ending in `DecoderLayer`.
  - `_make_phimoe_builder()` – `Phi3MoELongRoPEModel` subclass overriding `load_weights` to return the synthetic model, keeping tests fully offline without `trust_remote_code`.
  - `test_phimoe_onnx_build_cpu` – CPU-safe: builds ONNX graph and verifies I/O structure via `onnx.load` (no ORT/CUDA needed).
  - `test_phimoe_int4_cuda_build_and_run` – `@requires_cuda()`: builds ONNX, creates ORT session, runs prefill + decode, asserts output shapes. QMoE is CUDA-only so all inference tests are gated.

## Notes

The real `microsoft/Phi-3.5-MoE-instruct` model loads via `trust_remote_code=True` with a custom `block_sparse_moe` structure (`gate` + per-expert `w1/w2/w3`) that differs from HuggingFace's standard `PhimoeForCausalLM`. The synthetic model replicates that structure directly, matching the builder's expectations without any network access.

#### 41894db0ac68ab9f13087416e2579726077cee8f 
[BFCache] Add multi-process suspension for BFCache with Site Isolation
https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=311224
rdar://173743585

Reviewed by Sihui Liu.

When site isolation is active and multi-process BFCache is enabled, suspend
subframe processes alongside the main frame when a page enters the
back/forward cache. Each subframe process receives a SetSubframesSuspended
IPC — along with the main frame's BackForwardFrameItemIdentifier — that
caches its page in the WebCore BackForwardCache. A CallbackAggregator tracks
completion across all processes; if any fails, the BFCache entry is removed
and teardown cleans up the subframe processes.

The UIProcess passes fromItem->mainFrameItem().identifier() to each iframe
process. This identifier is unique per navigation entry, stable across iframe
cross-site navigations, and the same for all iframe processes — no
per-process frame tree traversal needed. Each iframe process stores its
CachedPage under this key in its own per-process BackForwardCache singleton.

Also refactor BackForwardCache::addIfCacheable to share logic between the
existing HistoryItem-based overload and the new identifier-based overload
used by iframe processes.

author: adamgauthier
body:
The passopt loop builds -e KEY=VALUE arguments for docker run by expanding the variable inline: -e %%i=!%%i!

When a value contains spaces (e.g. SQITCH_FULLNAME=Foo Bar), this produces an unquoted argument that Docker misparses:
  -e SQITCH_FULLNAME=Foo Bar
Docker treats 'Bar' as a positional argument (image name), causing: invalid reference format: repository name (library/Bar) must be lowercase

Use Docker's inherit syntax (-e "VARNAME") instead of explicitly constructing -e KEY=VALUE. This tells Docker to read the value from the host environment, which:
- Fixes spaces in values (the original bug)
- Avoids all cmd.exe quoting edge cases (quotes, !, &, etc.)
- Matches docker-sqitch.sh which already uses -e "$var" (inherit from host) on line 46

author: juppytt
body:
## Summary
Removes the full \`npm test\` step from \`.github/workflows/publish.yml\`. The publish workflow now does \`tsc --noEmit\` + \`npm pack --dry-run\` only, then publishes.

## Why

First v0.3.1 publish attempt failed at the test step, not the publish step. Root cause is a real bug in \`src/proxy/mitm.ts\`:

\`\`\`
gh stderr: Post \"https://api.github.com/graphql\": EOF
\`\`\`

\`gh issue view\` makes two GraphQL requests on the same keep-alive connection. The MITM proxy's \`handleInterceptedRequest\` calls \`tlsSocket.end()\` after the first response, so the second request races against the close and fails with EOF. Same root cause for the intermittent \`gws gmail +reply-all\` failure.

That's a real bug to fix (tracked separately), but it shouldn't be blocking releases.

## Why removing tests from publish.yml is fine

\`ci.yml\` already runs the full unit + e2e suite on every PR. By the time a tag exists pointing at a merge commit, that exact tree has already been validated. Re-running the same tests in the publish workflow:
- Adds no new safety (same tree, same tests)
- Adds release-blocking flake risk
- Slows publishes (~21s → ~5s)

The few things \`publish.yml\` should validate that \`ci.yml\` doesn't:
- TypeScript still compiles (\`tsc --noEmit\`)
- The \`files\` manifest still produces a valid tarball (\`npm pack --dry-run\`)

Both are kept.

## Followup

After this PR merges, the plan (per agreement with maintainer) is to **move the existing v0.3.1 tag to the new merge commit and force-push it** (Option A from the discussion). The dead first attempt is harmless and the version stays at 0.3.1.

## Test plan
- [ ] PR's \`ci.yml\` run is green (validates the underlying tree is still healthy)
- [ ] After merge + tag move: \`publish.yml\` succeeds
- [ ] \`@juppytt/fws@0.3.1\` appears on npmjs.com with provenance attestation

author: skogta
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! -->

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

The CSI controller watches CSINode objects via an informer. When the UUID is populated for the first time, csiNodeUpdate fires and calls RegisterNode, which:

Calls DiscoverNode → contacts vCenter via to find the VM by UUID
On success, stores nodeUUID → VirtualMachine in nodeVMs map
RegisterNode Stores nodeName → nodeUUID in nodeNameToUUID map
Both entries are required for GetAllNodes to return the node, which is in turn required by CreateVolume → GetSharedDatastoresInK8SCluster.

csiNodeUpdate only fires when the node UUID changes. Once the UUID was set (empty → populated), it never changed again, so the event never re-fired. There is no periodic reconciliation loop and no retry mechanism — a single failure permanently leaves the node unregistered for the lifetime of that pod.

To fix this, we should restart CSI driver whenever Node registration fails as this a P0 requirement for most of the volume operations.



**Testing done**:

Did basic sanity testing where I was able to create volumes with the new image.

Precheckin pipeline has passed: https://jenkins-vcf-csifvt.devops.broadcom.net/view/instapp/job/vanilla-instapp-e2e-pre-checkin/326/

author: nicolaturcato
body:
## Summary

Adds a new top-level `tsImportExtension` config option that appends a file extension to relative import paths in generated TypeScript files.

**Problem:** TypeScript 6 deprecated `moduleResolution: "node10"`, and TypeScript 7 will remove it entirely. Projects using `"nodenext"` or `"node16"` resolution require explicit `.js` extensions on relative imports — but gotsrpc currently generates extensionless imports like:

```typescript
import * as foo from './vo-constants';
```

**Solution:** When `tsImportExtension: ".js"` is set in the YAML config, generated imports become:

```typescript
import * as foo from './vo-constants.js';
```

The option defaults to `""` (empty string), so **existing behavior is unchanged** — this is fully backwards compatible.

## Usage

```yaml
module:
  name: github.com/example/project
  path: ./

tsImportExtension: ".js"

targets:
  # ...
mappings:
  # ...
```

## Changes

- **`config/config.go`** — Add `TSImportExtension` field to `Config` struct
- **`internal/build/build.go`** — Pass `conf.TSImportExtension` through `relativeFilePath()` → appended after stripping `.ts`
- **`gotsrpc.schema.json`** — Add `tsImportExtension` to the JSON schema

## Why this matters

- TypeScript 7 will remove `moduleResolution: "node10"` — projects need `"nodenext"` or `"bundler"`
- `"nodenext"` requires `.js` extensions on relative imports
- Without this option, consumers must post-process generated files with sed/scripts
- `.js` extensions are valid across **all** TS resolution modes, so opting in is always safe
