body:
## What

work on issue #947.

Closes #947

## Artifacts

| File | Path |
|------|------|
| Plan | `.flow-states/extractimplementationplan-uses-plan.md` |
| DAG | `.flow-states/extractimplementationplan-uses-dag.md` |
| Log | `.flow-states/extractimplementationplan-uses.log` |
| State | `.flow-states/extractimplementationplan-uses.json` |
| Transcript | `/Users/ben/.claude/projects/-Users-ben-code-flow/5e919f5a-73b3-4bd8-9583-55fbff5e54f2.jsonl` |

## Plan

<details>
<summary>Implementation plan</summary>

```text
## Context

Issue #947: `extract_implementation_plan` in `src/plan_extract.rs:184-201` uses `body.find("## Implementation Plan")` which is a substring match. Any heading that starts with `## Implementation Plan` followed by additional characters (e.g., `## Implementation Planning`) will falsely match and extract the wrong section.

## Exploration

- **Bug location**: `src/plan_extract.rs:186` — `body.find(marker)` where `marker = "## Implementation Plan"`. `String::find` is a substring match, not a full-heading match.
- **Call site**: Single caller at `src/plan_extract.rs:471`.
- **End-of-section marker** (lines 191-193): Uses `find("\n## ")` which already includes line-start boundary (`\n`) and trailing space. This is sound and does not need changes.
- **Existing tests**: `tests/plan_extract.rs` has 9 unit tests and 6 integration tests. None test the false-positive substring match case.
- **No existing `find_heading` helper**: Grep confirmed no similar helper exists in the codebase.
- **Public API**: `extract_implementation_plan` is `pub` and imported in tests — new test cases can exercise it directly.

## Risks

- **Existing test regression**: The fix must not break any of the 15 existing tests. All existing tests use `## Implementation Plan` followed by `\n`, so a full-heading match will continue to match them correctly.
- **Code block edge case**: The existing `extract_plan_ends_at_first_h2` test documents an accepted limitation (line 104-106 comment). The fix must not alter the end-of-section behavior.
- **String slicing safety**: The `find_heading` helper uses byte-level checks (`body.as_bytes()[idx]`). Since `\n`, `\r` are single-byte ASCII characters, byte indexing is safe here per `.claude/rules/rust-patterns.md`.

## Approach

Add a private `find_heading(body, heading)` helper function that performs a full-heading match:
1. Check if `body` starts with the heading AND the next character is `\n`, `\r`, or end of string
2. Search for `\n` + heading occurrences, checking that each candidate also ends at a line boundary
3. Return `Some(index)` of the heading start position, or `None`

Replace `body.find(marker)` with `find_heading(body, marker)` in `extract_implementation_plan`. The rest of the function (end-of-section logic, trim, empty check) remains unchanged.

## Dependency Graph

| Task | Type | Depends On |
|------|------|------------|
| 1. Write tests for false-positive and true-positive cases | test | — |
| 2. Add `find_heading` helper and update `extract_implementation_plan` | implement | 1 |

## Tasks

### Task 1: Write tests for substring match false positives and true positives

**File**: `tests/plan_extract.rs`

Add 6 new unit tests after the existing `extract_plan_ends_at_first_h2` test (line 113):

- `extract_plan_rejects_heading_suffix` — body with `## Implementation Planning\n\n### Context\n\nStuff.\n` should return `None`
- `extract_plan_rejects_heading_extra_words` — body with `## Implementation Plan Details\n\n### Context\n\nStuff.\n` should return `None`
- `extract_plan_rejects_mid_line_heading` — body with `some text ## Implementation Plan\n\n### Context\n\nStuff.\n` should return `None`
- `extract_plan_matches_at_start_of_body` — body starting with `## Implementation Plan\n\n### Context\n\nStuff.\n` should return `Some`
- `extract_plan_matches_at_end_of_body` — body ending with `\n## Implementation Plan` (no trailing newline) should return `Some("")` → actually `None` since empty. Use `\n## Implementation Plan\n\n### Context\n\nContent.` instead
- `extract_plan_matches_windows_line_endings` — body with `## Implementation Plan\r\n\n### Context\n\nStuff.\n` should return `Some`

**TDD**: These tests will fail initially since `extract_implementation_plan` currently uses substring matching.

### Task 2: Add `find_heading` helper and update `extract_implementation_plan`

**File**: `src/plan_extract.rs`

- Add a private `fn find_heading(body: &str, heading: &str) -> Option<usize>` helper before `extract_implementation_plan`
- The helper checks line-start boundary (preceded by `\n` or at position 0) AND line-end boundary (followed by `\n`, `\r`, or end of string)
- Replace `body.find(marker)?` at line 186 with `find_heading(body, marker)?`
- Update the doc comment on `extract_implementation_plan` to mention it uses full-heading matching
- Run `bin/flow ci` to verify all existing + new tests pass
```

</details>

## DAG Analysis

<details>
<summary>Decompose plugin output</summary>

````text
# DAG Analysis: Fix extract_implementation_plan substring match bug

```xml
<dag goal="Fix extract_implementation_plan substring match bug — replace body.find() with full-heading match" mode="full">
  <plan>
    <node id="1" name="Read Current Implementation" type="research" depends="[]" parallel_with="[]">
      <objective>Read src/plan_extract.rs to understand the exact matching logic and all callers of extract_implementation_plan</objective>
    </node>
    <node id="2" name="Analyze Match Semantics" type="analysis" depends="[1]" parallel_with="3">
      <objective>Determine what constitutes a "full heading match" for ## Implementation Plan — what characters can follow the heading text</objective>
    </node>
    <node id="3" name="Find All Heading Matches" type="research" depends="[1]" parallel_with="2">
      <objective>Search codebase for all places that match or reference "## Implementation Plan" to understand the full contract</objective>
    </node>
    <node id="4" name="Identify End-of-Section Pattern" type="analysis" depends="[1]" parallel_with="2,3">
      <objective>Examine how the function finds the END of the Implementation Plan section — does the same substring bug affect the end marker?</objective>
    </node>
    <node id="5" name="Synthesize Fix and Test Plan" type="synthesis" depends="[2,3,4]" parallel_with="[]">
      <objective>Design the fix, enumerate edge cases, and define test coverage</objective>
    </node>
  </plan>

```

---

▶ NODE 1: Read Current Implementation (depends on: none)

Read `src/plan_extract.rs` — full file (610 lines). The function in question:

```rust
pub fn extract_implementation_plan(body: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let marker = "## Implementation Plan";
    let start_idx = body.find(marker)?;
    let after_marker = start_idx + marker.len();

    // Find the next ## heading after the marker
    let content_after = &body[after_marker..];
    let end_offset = content_after
        .find("\n## ")
        .map(|pos| after_marker + pos)
        .unwrap_or(body.len());

    let section = body[after_marker..end_offset].trim().to_string();
    if section.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    Some(section)
}
```

Called at one site: line 471 in the same file.

Quality: 9/10 — Full function visible, bug confirmed at line 186.

Key finding: `body.find("## Implementation Plan")` at line 186 is a substring match — `"## Implementation Planning"`, `"## Implementation Plan Details"`, etc. would all match.

---

▶ PARALLEL BRANCH A — NODE 2: Analyze Match Semantics (depends on: 1)

A markdown `## Implementation Plan` heading is a full line. Valid forms:
- `## Implementation Plan\n` — heading followed by newline
- `## Implementation Plan\r\n` — Windows line endings
- `## Implementation Plan` at end of string (no trailing newline)

What must NOT match:
- `## Implementation Planning` — different heading
- `## Implementation Plan Details` — different heading
- `some text ## Implementation

body:
💡 **What:** Refactored `load_sources`, `save_metadata`, and `main` in `Scripts/update_lists.py` to use asynchronous I/O (`aiofiles` and `asyncio.to_thread`) instead of synchronous blocking calls.

🎯 **Why:** Synchronous file I/O in an `async` function blocks the event loop, causing jitter and reducing the overall efficiency of the download pipeline, especially when handling many sources.

📊 **Measured Improvement:** Using a benchmark with 10,000 sources, the execution time for `load_sources` was reduced from **0.0432s** (blocking) to **0.0326s** (non-blocking), representing a **~25%** improvement in processing speed and, more importantly, the elimination of event loop blocking.

author: janedbal
body:
## Summary
- When `#[AutowireIterator]`, `#[TaggedIterator]`, `#[TaggedLocator]` or `#[AutowireLocator]` used a **string tag** (e.g. `'app.handler'`) instead of a class FQCN, the `defaultIndexMethod`/`defaultPriorityMethod` targets were falsely reported as dead
- Now we build a tag-to-classes map from `<tag>` elements in the DIC XML and use it to resolve string tags to concrete service classes
- Also fixes `#[AutowireLocator]` when its `$services` parameter is a string (tag name) rather than an array of class references

### Note

String tag resolution requires the container XML to be configured (same as other DIC-based features). This is done via either:
- [`phpstan/phpstan-symfony`](https://github.com/phpstan/phpstan-symfony) with `containerXmlPath`
- `shipmonkDeadCode.usageProviders.symfony.containerXmlPaths` configured directly:

```neon
parameters:
    shipmonkDeadCode:
        usageProviders:
            symfony:
                containerXmlPaths:
                    - %rootDir%/../../../var/cache/dev/App_KernelDevDebugContainer.xml
```

When a class FQCN is used as the tag (e.g. `#[AutowireIterator(SomeInterface::class, defaultIndexMethod: 'method')]`), it continues to work without any XML configuration.

Fixes #335

body:
Added std::map functionality to the existing Climbing Activity Tracker program.

What I changed :
-Added #include <map> to the headers

member of ActivityManager
- The map key is the difficulty string(Easy, Moderate, Hard, Extreme)
and the value is the count of activities at that difficulty
- Updated add(), addToFront(), remove(), and clear() to keep
the map in sync with the linked list automatically
- Added getDifficultyCount() for lookup
- Added displayDifficultyMap() for iteration and display
- Added deleteDifficultyFromMap() for explicit key deletion
- Integrated map display into generateReport()
- Added menu option 8 to view difficulty counts from the menu
- Added 8 new tests covering all map operations and edge cases

Why choose map :
A map gives instant O(log n) lookup by difficulty name without
looping through all activities.This enhances the existing program
by making difficulty based reporting faster and cleaner.

author: apoupard
body:
## Summary
- The `version` composite action's `with-snapshot-tag` input defaults to `.${GITHUB_SHA:0:7}`, but the literal string was being written into the `VERSION` file without bash evaluating the substring expansion.
- Downstream Makefiles run under `/bin/sh` (dash on Ubuntu runners), which does not support the `${VAR:offset:length}` syntax and fails with `Bad substitution`.
- Evaluate the snapshot tag with `eval printf` before substitution so the `VERSION` file always contains a fully resolved string.

## Context
This bug surfaces in any consumer that uses `make-kotlin-npm-workflow.yml` (or any workflow passing `use-snapshot: false` with the default snapshot tag). Example failure observed in komune-io/connect-im's `kotkin-js / run-dev-tasks` job:

```
VERSION=0.23.0.${GITHUB_SHA:0:7} ./gradlew :im-f2:apikey:im-apikey-domain:build
/bin/sh: 1: Bad substitution
make: *** [infra/make/libsJs.mk:9: build] Error 2
```

## Test plan
- [x] Local repro: `GITHUB_SHA=abc1234567890 SNAPSHOT_TAG='.${GITHUB_SHA:0:7}' bash -c 'SNAPSHOT_TAG_EXPANDED=$(eval "printf '\''%s'\'' \"$SNAPSHOT_TAG\""); echo "$SNAPSHOT_TAG_EXPANDED"'` yields `.abc1234`
- [ ] Re-run the `kotkin-js` job on a downstream PR (e.g. komune-io/connect-im#117) after this change is merged, pointing the consumer workflows at this branch

author: luyao618
body:
## What does this PR do?

Prevents Slack image/audio downloads from silently caching HTML sign-in pages as media files. When Slack returns an HTML response instead of actual media (e.g. due to expired bot tokens), the raw HTML bytes were written to the image cache as `.png`/`.jpg` files, causing downstream `vision_analyze` to fail with confusing errors.

This PR adds two-layer content validation to `_download_slack_file()` **before** writing to cache:
1. **Content-Type check** — reject responses with `text/html` or `text/xml` headers
2. **Magic-byte check** — verify the payload starts with a known image or audio file signature (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WEBP, BMP, OGG, MP3, FLAC, WAV)

If either check fails, a clear `ValueError` is raised, which the caller's existing `except` block logs as a descriptive warning — no silent corruption.

## Related Issue

Fixes #6829

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/platforms/slack.py` — Added `_looks_like_media()` (magic-byte validator), `_content_type_is_html()` (header check), and integrated both into `_download_slack_file()` between `raise_for_status()` and the cache write
- `tests/gateway/test_slack_image_cache.py` — **New**: 27 tests covering magic-byte recognition, Content-Type detection, download validation (HTML rejected, valid media accepted, garbage bytes rejected), and end-to-end message handling with invalid media
- `tests/gateway/test_media_download_retry.py` — Updated 2 existing tests to use valid JPEG magic bytes (they previously used `b"fake image bytes"` which now correctly fails validation)

## How to Test

1. `pytest tests/gateway/test_slack_image_cache.py -v` — all 27 new tests pass
2. `pytest tests/gateway/test_media_download_retry.py -v` — all existing retry tests still pass
3. `pytest tests/gateway/test_slack.py -v` — all existing Slack adapter tests still pass
4. `pytest tests/ -q --ignore=tests/integration --ignore=tests/e2e` — full test suite passes (no new failures)

author: f-liva
body:
## Summary

The `cli_profile_dirs` rotation guard introduced in #2249 only matches `provider == "claude_code"` (underscore), but the documented and commonly used provider name in config.toml is `"claude-code"` (hyphen). This causes profile rotation to silently not activate.

**Two guards were affected:**
1. **Init guard** (kernel boot) — rotation pool created but condition check failed
2. **Dispatch guard** (`get_or_create_driver_for_agent()`) — even if the pool was created, every agent call created a single driver instead of using the TokenRotationDriver pool

## Problem

```toml
[default_model]
provider = "claude-code"  # ← hyphen, as documented
cli_profile_dirs = ["~/.claude", "~/.claude-profiles/account-2"]
```

The kernel creates the rotation pool at boot, but the dispatch guard in `get_or_create_driver_for_agent()` checks `provider == "claude_code"` — guard fails, a fresh single ClaudeCodeDriver is created per call, bypassing the rotation pool entirely.

## Fix

Both guards now use `matches!()` with both variants:

```rust
matches!(
    effective_default.provider.as_str(),
    "claude_code" | "claude-code"
)
```

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo check -p librefang-kernel` passes
- [x] Verified on production deployment with `provider = "claude-code"` and 3 profiles
- [x] Confirmed rotation logs show all 3 profiles being tried (`Key exhausted, entering cooldown profile=profile-1/2/3`)
- [x] Before fix: only 1 "CLI exited with error" per attempt (single driver). After fix: 3 attempts visible in logs (rotation working)

author: claycantrell
body:
## Summary

When patrol scan detects dead polecats with hooked beads, notify the mayor — not just the witness. This closes the notification gap where polecats dying from context exhaustion or crashes went completely unnoticed.

## What changed

- `sendZombieNotification` now sends mail to `mayor/` in addition to the witness
- Mayor mail includes bead IDs and resling instructions
- Notification is automatic for active-work zombies (was `--notify` flag only)

## Why

The detection infrastructure exists (heartbeats, zombie classification, `DetectZombiePolecats`) but the notification only went to the witness, which logs it to stderr and moves on. The mayor — who slung the work and needs to resling failures — was never told.

Real-world impact: in a session today, 2/3 polecats died from context exhaustion. Work sat stranded for 15+ minutes until manual tmux inspection.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...` compiles clean
- [ ] E2E: kill a polecat mid-work, run `gt patrol scan`, verify mayor gets mail
- [ ] Verify witness still gets its notification too

Fixes #3584

## Description
OpenAPI does not define format: hex ([data types](https://swagger.io/docs/specification/data-models/data-types/#string)); some tools error on it (see [#297](https://github.com/symbol/symbol-openapi/issues/297)).

Changes: use pattern: '^[0-9a-fA-F]+$' for hex strings and keep fixed sizes with minLength / maxLength (length not duplicated in the regex). Add missing length bounds where fields are fixed-size. Update route examples so hex values (e.g. signatures) match those constraints.

### Signature and examples problem

There’s an issue with the ``signature`` where I should enforce a length constraint (min and max: 128). However, this would cause validation failures with the current examples - I had to shorten them earlier because the linter was already failing. For now, I’ll leave it without the constraint and revisit it later, once I verify whether the linting rules can be relaxed after moving to the monorepo.

body:
## Summary
This PR introduces text formatting presets and expands typography control options in the presentation editor. Users can now quickly apply predefined text styles (Heading, Subheading, Body, Caption, Quote) and have fine-grained control over text alignment, line height, and letter spacing.

## Key Changes

- **Text Presets System**: Added `textPreset` type with five predefined styles (Heading, Subheading, Body, Caption, Quote), each with configured font size, weight, style, line height, letter spacing, and default dimensions
- **Extended Text Properties**: Added `textAlign`, `lineHeight`, and `letterSpacing` to `textProps` record for more granular typography control
- **Preset Application**: 
  - `makeTextElementFromPreset()` creates text elements with preset styling
  - `applyPreset()` applies preset styles to existing text elements
  - `getPresetConfig()` and `presetLabel()` helper functions for preset management
- **UI Enhancements**:
  - Text button in toolbar now opens a dropdown menu showing all preset options with live preview styling
  - Properties panel includes preset buttons for quick style application
  - Added text alignment buttons (Left, Center, Right) with visual feedback
  - Added input controls for line height and letter spacing
- **Persistence**: Updated JSON serialization/deserialization to preserve new typography properties across save/load cycles
- **Rendering Updates**: Canvas, Presenter, and SlidePanel components now apply the new typography properties (text alignment, line height, letter spacing) to rendered text

## Implementation Details

- Preset configurations are centralized in `DeckData.res` for easy maintenance
- All new properties use `Signal.t` for reactive updates
- Dropdown menu includes a backdrop click handler to close the menu
- Preset menu items display with their actual styling for visual preview
- Default values ensure backward compatibility with existing presentations

This pull request introduces a new interactive preview for the Tabs component, enhances the documentation in both German and English, and adds internationalization support for the new features. The main changes are the addition of a `TabsPreview` component and an editable `TabsProperty` for live editing of tab properties, along with updates to the documentation to use these new components.

**Component Preview and Property Editing Enhancements:**

* Added a new `TabsPreview` component (`src/components/previews/components/Tabs.tsx`) that provides an interactive, configurable preview of the Tabs component, allowing users to adjust properties and see changes live.
* Introduced `TabsProperty` (`src/components/previews/properties/TabsProperty.tsx`) for editing tab properties (label, icon, tooltip alignment, disabled state, hide label) via a drawer UI, including tab count adjustment and per-tab editing.
* Registered `TabsProperty` in the property components index for use in previews.

author: nelzonmamani
body:
### Motivation
- Close remaining execution gaps by deterministically reconciling local tracked positions, broker position callbacks, and cumulative `execDetails` fills to surface mismatches and lifecycle evidence. 
- Detect and classify stalled / no-ack / no-fill orders with a lightweight watchdog so stalled cases are visible and can be escalated safely without auto-cancelling. 
- Make IBKR health recovery non-sticky by tracking sub-channel health and emitting explicit recovery evidence so transient errors can be cleared when broker evidence returns.

### Description
- Implemented broker-authoritative position reconciliation inside `src/execution/order_router.py` that compares local positions, broker positions, and cumulative local fills to emit verdicts (`ALIGNED`, `BROKER_POSITION_WITHOUT_FILL`, `LOCAL_FILL_WITHOUT_BROKER_POSITION`, `QTY_MISMATCH`, `AVG_COST_MISMATCH`, `POSITION_CLOSED_ALIGNED`, `UNKNOWN_PENDING_RECONCILIATION`) plus structured logs (`[EXECUTION][POSITION_RECONCILE]`, `[EXECUTION][POSITION_RECONCILE_MISMATCH]`, `[EXECUTION][POSITION_RECONCILE_OK]`) and counters (`reconciled_positions_ok`, `reconciled_positions_mismatch`, `broker_position_without_fill_count`, `local_fill_without_position_count`).
- Added a stuck-order watchdog with configurable thresholds (`EXECUTION_SUBMIT_TO_ACK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, `EXECUTION_ACK_TO_WORKING_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, `EXECUTION_WORKING_NO_FILL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, `EXECUTION_PARTIAL_FILL_STALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`) and classification (`SUBMITTED_NO_ACK_TIMEOUT`, `ACKNOWLEDGED_NO_WORKING_TIMEOUT`, `WORKING_NO_FILL_TIMEOUT`, `PARTIAL_FILL_STALLED`, `HEALTH_BLOCKED_PENDING`, `NORMAL_IN_FLIGHT`), emitted logs (`[EXECUTION][WATCHDOG]`, `[EXECUTION][WATCHDOG_STALL]`), escalation flags on `TrackedOrder`, and counters (`watchdog_stalls_total`, `submitted_no_ack_timeouts`, `working_no_fill_timeouts`, `partial_fill_stalls`).
- Extended IBKR health semantics to track sub-state recovery, `recovered_at`, `last_recovery_codes` and emit `[IBKR][HEALTH_RECOVERY]` when channels return to healthy, while keeping degradation conservative and non-sticky; also added post-fill and position lifecycle evidence logs (`[EXECUTION][FILL_CONFIRMED]`, lifecycle markers `FILL_CONFIRMED_AWAITING_POSITION`, `POSITION_OPEN_CONFIRMED`, `POSITION_REDUCED_CONFIRMED`, `POSITION_CLOSED_CONFIRMED`).
- Added cycle-end reconciliation summary output (`[EXECUTION][RECONCILIATION_SUMMARY]`) and extended `runtime_lifecycle_snapshot()` to expose the new counters and states, updated `TrackedOrder` with timestamp fields and escalation metadata, and added tests in `tests/test_execution_reconciliation_watchdog.py`.

### Testing
- Ran the targeted unit tests with `pytest -q tests/test_execution_truth_state_machine.py tests/test_execution_reconciliation_watchdog.py`. 
- All targeted tests passed (`10 passed`). 
- The new tests exercise position reconciliation verdicts, watchdog classification, IBKR health recovery emission, post-fill lifecycle evidence, and the reconciliation summary log.

author: cyrusnajmabadi
body:
## Summary

Add an approximate count field to `InjectionQueue` with a `Volatile.Read` fast-reject in `TryDequeue`. Workers call `TryDequeue` on every `TryExecuteOne` fallback when local pop and steal both fail. In saturated workloads the injection queue is almost always empty, but every worker was acquiring the lock just to discover this. The `Volatile.Read` converts that lock acquisition to a single acquire load.

Changes to `InjectionQueue`:
- New `_approximateCount` field, incremented under lock in `Enqueue`/`EnqueueBatch`, decremented in `TryDequeue`, zeroed in `DrainToList`
- `TryDequeue` fast-rejects with `Volatile.Read(ref _approximateCount) <= 0` before taking the lock

## Benchmark Results (32 phases × 192 jobs, 12,500 compute iterations)

|  | Mean | Median | P95 | Lock Contentions |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Master** | 4.862 ms | 4.692 ms | 5.591 ms | 37.56 |
| **This PR** | 4.586 ms | 4.583 ms | 4.752 ms | 0 |
| **Δ** | −5.7% | −2.3% | −15.0% | −100% |

Raw BDN output:

| Method | Mean | Error | StdDev | Median | P95 | Op/s | Completed Work Items | Lock Contentions | Allocated |
| -------- | ---------:|----------:|----------:|---------:|---------:|------:|---------------------:|-----------------:|----------:|
| OneTick | 4.586 ms | 0.1209 ms | 0.1072 ms | 4.583 ms | 4.752 ms | 218.1 | - | - | - |

## JIT Disassembly Analysis

### No-PGO code size changes

| Method | Master | Branch | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| PushToRingBuffer | 560 | 592 | +32 (overflow path increments count) |
| RunWorker | 2224 | 2696 | +472 (Volatile.Read fast-reject inlined) |
| RunUntilComplete | 448 | 480 | +32 |

### PGO impact

Lock-related references in RunWorker OSR body halved (12 → 6). The `TryDequeue` fast path now emits a single `ldapr` (acquire load) + `cmp` + conditional branch, skipping the lock acquisition entirely when the count is zero.

author: stffns
body:
💡 **What:** Added a dynamic, vectorized `delete_batch` monkey-patch to `snapvec.SnapIndex` inside `vstash/store.py` (guarded so it doesn't overwrite future upstream implementations). Replaced the loop invoking `self._snap.delete(cid)` with `self._snap.delete_batch(chunk_ids)`.

🎯 **Why:** The previous iterative deletion logic performed an O(N) array reallocation (`np.delete`) per vector during document removal, leading to extreme slowness when deleting documents with many chunks. The new method uses a boolean mask to delete them in a single batch pass.

📊 **Measured Improvement:** In a local benchmark script deleting 1,000 vectors from an index of 10,000 vectors, time dropped from ~1.82s (sequential) to ~0.0055s (batch), representing an ~330x speedup for in-memory index deletions.

🔬 **Measurement:** Measured directly via `time.perf_counter()` on the standalone `snapvec` class with generated vectors.

author: aki1770-del
body:
Closes #493

## Problem

When a VSS signal has `datatype: string` and an `allowed` attribute, the protobuf exporter emits a plain `string` field. This silently accepts any value at the protobuf layer — the constraint declared in the VSS spec is invisible to protobuf consumers.

```python
# Before — allowed values ['DRY', 'WET', 'SNOW', 'ICE'] are lost
string Surface = 2;
```

## Fix

`print_messages()` now uses a two-pass approach in `src/vss_tools/exporters/protobuf.py`:

- **Pass 1**: for each `string` + `allowed` field, emit a nested `enum <FieldName>Enum` with allowed values assigned indices starting at 0 (satisfying the proto3 zero-value requirement).
- **Pass 2**: emit the field using the enum type instead of `string`.

`repeated string[]` fields with `allowed` become `repeated <EnumType>`. String fields without `allowed` and all non-string fields are unchanged.

```proto
# After
message A {
  enum SurfaceEnum {
    DRY = 0;
    WET = 1;
    SNOW = 2;
    ICE = 3;
  }
  repeated SurfaceEnum Surface = 2;
}
```

**Note on proto3 zero-value semantics**: proto3 uses the first enum entry as the default for unset fields. This implementation assigns index 0 to the first entry in the VSS `allowed` list. For signals that follow the convention of listing `UNKNOWN` first (e.g., `Vehicle.Exterior.RoadSurfaceCondition`), this aligns naturally. For signals without a natural "unset" first value, the first allowed entry becomes the proto default. Happy to discuss if a different index assignment strategy is preferred.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/vss_tools/exporters/protobuf.py` | +33 lines — `_enum_type_name()`, `_write_nested_enum()`, two-pass logic in `print_messages()` |
| `tests/vspec/test_protobuf_enum_allowed/` | New test: scalar, repeated, and unchanged-float cases |
| `tests/vspec/test_protobuf_comments/expected_*.proto` | Updated expected output to reflect enum generation for `StringWithAllowed` fixture |

## Tests

```
$ python3 -m pytest tests/ -k "proto" -v
13 passed in 5.36s
```

All 13 protobuf-related tests pass, including the two existing `test_protobuf_comments` parametrized cases (no-comments / with-comments) which already contained a `string` + `allowed` field in their fixture.

*AI-assisted — authored with Claude, reviewed by Komada.*

## Summary

Closes the three zero-coverage gaps and three documentation errors flagged by test-audit (#141). All work was driven through the scrum lifecycle (plan → plan-review → implement → code-review → closeout → learn) for each subtask.

- **+36 unit tests** across three previously zero-coverage modules (optics physics, C API result getters, SimData/RayBuffer)
- **+1 DISABLED contract anchor** locking a known batch `EmplaceBack` quirk for future fix
- **3 doc fixes** (CI artifact name, E2E test filename, nonexistent `conftest.py` reference) applied symmetrically to English and Chinese docs

| Module | New tests | File |
|--------|-----------|------|

## Description

Implements the full authentication journey (Flow 2) for the Herit portal:

- **MSAL redirect handling** — `main.tsx` now wraps `RouterProvider` in an `AppShell` that shows `AuthLoadingPage` during `InteractionStatus.HandleRedirect` and `AuthErrorPage` on `LOGIN_FAILURE`, globally before the router mounts.
- **AuthLoadingPage** — animated spinner card matching design `01-loading.html`.
- **AuthErrorPage** — error card with "Try Again" (re-triggers `loginRedirect`) and "Return to Browse" (`globalThis.location.href = '/'`, safe before router mount) matching design `02-auth-error.html`.
- **CompleteProfilePage** — JIT profile completion form. Pre-populates email (read-only) and full name from MSAL account. Collects nationality, location, expertise tags, and mandatory terms checkbox. On submit calls `PATCH /Users/{id}/profile` with `termsAcceptedAt`, then invalidates `currentUser` query and navigates to `/dashboard`.
- **DashboardPage** — two visual states: new-user (empty state + dismissible session-only welcome banner) and returning-user (proposal cards + EOI list). Proposals filtered client-side by `authorId === user.id` (TODO comment noting missing backend filter). EOIs via `listMyEois`.
- **useCurrentUser** — fixed to call `GET /Users/me` (JWT-identified endpoint) instead of the broken admin-only `GET /Users/{id}`. Exposes `isNotFound` flag for 404 handling.

author: cyrilsbrodov
body:
### Motivation
- The existing torch scaffold was too lightweight: tensor batch surface and mode semantics were insufficient to support real learned renderers.
- Reveal/insertion/update paths were nearly identical and did not receive structured, path-specific conditioning needed for learning.
- Checkpoint and backend readiness semantics were loose, allowing random/uninitialized weights to be treated as usable learned backends, and trace visibility was weak.

### Description
- Expanded the training surface by enhancing `RendererTensorBatch` with `conditioning_map`, `reveal_signal`, `insertion_signal`, `region_geometry`, `conditioning_summary` and a richer `context_vector`, and updated `build_renderer_tensor_batch` to accept lifecycle/mode/entity/scene/insertion/reveal parameters. (files: `src/rendering/torch_backends.py`).
- Introduced FiLM-like path conditioning via `_PathConditioning` and made `_TorchPathModule` context-aware so each path gets real context-modulated features instead of a nominal shared pass. (files: `src/rendering/torch_backends.py`).
- Added strict checkpoint/readiness handling in `TorchRendererBackendBundle` with `checkpoint_status`/`checkpoint_details`, robust `load_checkpoint` validation (`checkpoint_loaded`, `checkpoint_file_missing`, `checkpoint_invalid`, `checkpoint_directory_missing`), and centralized `backend_runtime_status` plus `allow_random_init_for_dev` guard. (files: `src/rendering/torch_backends.py`).
- Wired path-specific conditioning into orchestration in `PatchRenderer`/path implementations so `existing`, `reveal`, and `insertion` build and pass structured batch features and include `backend_runtime_status` and `tensor_conditioning_summary` into execution traces; insertion now derives `insertion_score` from real context instead of fixed constants. (files: `src/rendering/roi_renderer.py`).
- Tests updated/added to reflect tightened contracts and behaviour: `tests/test_renderer_torch_backends.py` now asserts richer tensor shapes, distinct mode features, strict backend usability policy, and correct checkpoint trace handling. (files: `tests/test_renderer_torch_backends.py`).

### Testing
- Ran `pytest -q tests/test_renderer_torch_backends.py` and the suite passed (checks for tensor surface, mode differences, usability policy, and checkpoint trace succeeded). 
- Ran `pytest -q tests/test_renderer_scene_modes.py` and it passed, confirming routing and high-level mode behavior remained compatible. 
- Attempted `pytest -q tests/test_integration_runtime_rendering.py` but collection failed in this environment due to missing `numpy` (import-time dependency), so integration-level checks were not executed here.

author: kamchihei
body:
### Motivation
- Forward dataflow currently iterates over all CFG nodes which can propagate facts into unreachable blocks and produce spurious results in some tests.
- Restricting the forward fixpoint iteration to nodes reachable from the CFG entry prevents analyzing dead/unreachable code paths and avoids incorrect fact propagation.

### Description
- Compute the set of nodes reachable from `cfg.getEntry()` using a BFS and store them in a `LinkedHashSet` to preserve traversal order.
- Seed the forward worklist from the reachable node set instead of iterating over the entire `cfg` collection.
- Keep the existing `meet`/`transfer` logic unchanged so only the node set considered by the forward solver is narrowed.
- Modified file: `A2/tai-e/src/main/java/pascal/taie/analysis/dataflow/solver/WorkListSolver.java`.

author: markuscouch
body:
### Motivation

- Sicherstellen, dass alle in `fetch_data/config.yml` konfigurierten Länder/Regionen/Kategorien tatsächlich GeoJSON-Ressourcen in `resources/geojson` haben. 
- Automatisches Erkennen von fehlenden Dateien in CI, damit Pull Requests nicht versehentlich unvollständige Datensätze einbringen.

### Description

- Neu: `scripts/check_missing_json.py` — ein Python‑3 Skript, das `fetch_data/config.yml` lädt, Kategorien (global und länderspezifisch) auflöst und erwartete Pfade für jede Kombination `country/region/category` ableitet und prüft (Verwendung von `pathlib` und `PyYAML`).
- Die Skriptlogik bevorzugt top‑level `regions` (mit `path`) zur Auflösung von Region‑Ordnern und fällt auf eingebettete `countries.<id>.regions` zurück; `query_mode: country-only` führt zu einem `<country>/<country>`-Fallback; bei ungültiger Config werden klare Fehler gemeldet.
- Fehlende Dateien werden nach Land gruppiert ausgegeben, mit einer übersichtlichen Zusammenfassung, und das Skript beendet sich mit `sys.exit(1)` wenn etwas fehlt, sonst mit `0` und einer Erfolgsmeldung.
- Neu: `.github/workflows/check-missing-json.yml` — GitHub Actions Workflow (triggert `workflow_dispatch`, `pull_request`, `push` auf `main`) der Repo auscheckt, Python 3.11 bereitstellt, Dependencies via `pip install -r fetch_data/requirements.txt` installiert und anschließend `python scripts/check_missing_json.py` ausführt.

### Testing

- `python -m py_compile scripts/check_missing_json.py` wurde erfolgreich ausgeführt und validierte die Syntax des Skripts.
- `python scripts/check_missing_json.py` wurde lokal ausgeführt und trat erwartungsgemäß mit Exit Code `1` aus, während es eine gruppierte Liste fehlender GeoJSON-Dateien und eine Zusammenfassung (z.B. `Missing JSON files ... Summary: 516 missing file(s) across 11 countr(ies).`) ausgab. 
- Der neue Workflow wurde als YAML-Datei erstellt und installiertiert Dependencies über `fetch_data/requirements.txt`, sodass der CI‑Lauf das gleiche Prüfskript ausführt (Workflow selbst wurde nicht in Actions ausgeführt hier, aber die Schritte sind minimal-invasiv und lauffähig).

author: hkd987
body:
Three parallel reviews (reuse, quality, efficiency) converged on a short
list of real issues. Fixes grouped by file:

advisor.ts
- Attach an 'error' listener to child.stdin so EPIPE (child exits before
  reading the full prompt) rejects the promise instead of crashing the
  entire MCP server process with an unhandled error event.
- Cap stdout+stderr buffering at maxOutputBytes (default 1 MiB). A runaway
  advisor that floods stdout now gets SIGKILL'd and the call rejects with
  "output exceeded N bytes" instead of OOMing the host.
- Switch stdout/stderr accumulation from string concat to Buffer[] +
  Buffer.concat (cleaner and the byte-accurate cap needs Buffer.length).
- Escalate SIGTERM -> SIGKILL after a 5s grace period on timeout so a
  wedged `claude` subprocess can't linger as a zombie. The escalation
  timer is .unref()'d so it doesn't block server shutdown.
- Reject (instead of silently resolving with "") when the child exits 0
  with no stdout. Sonnet now sees a real error rather than an empty
  advisor reply it might mistake for silent agreement.

config.ts
- Treat ADVISOR_MAX_CALLS="" (and whitespace-only) as "unset" instead of
  parsing to 0, which previously disabled the tool silently.
- Use Number.isInteger + >= 0, rejecting "1.5", "-1", and "abc" to the
  default (5) in one check.
- Broaden ADVISOR_ENABLED disabled matching to {"false","0","no","off"},
  case-insensitive and whitespace-trimmed. Previously only the exact
  string "false" disabled, so "FALSE" or "0" silently left it on.

index.ts
- Extract a textResult() helper and a ToolResult type. Collapses four
  duplicated `{ content: [{ type: "text" as const, text: ... }] }`
  literals into single-line call sites and removes the repeated `as
  const` assertions.
- Fix the budget race: reserve the slot (callCount += 1) BEFORE the
  await, not after, so two concurrent tool calls can't both pass the
  < maxCalls gate and overrun the budget. Failures still count against
  budget — a flaky advisor shouldn't enable unbounded retries.
- Reject whitespace-only context via z.string().refine(s => s.trim()...)
  instead of .min(1), which only checked raw length.
- Move the "stdio server ready" stderr log to BEFORE transport.connect()
  so there's no chance of a client parser observing it mid-handshake.

tests
- New test/config.test.ts covering model trim+fallback, empty/whitespace
  ADVISOR_MAX_CALLS, non-integer rejection, and the full ADVISOR_ENABLED
  casing matrix. Config had zero coverage before.
- Four new advisor.test.ts cases: stdin EPIPE, output-byte-cap kill,
  empty-stdout-on-exit-0 rejection, and idempotent settle under a late
  second close event. Total suite: 18/18 green.
- makeFakeChild now records kill signals so tests can assert the correct
  signal is sent on timeout / over-budget paths. Replaced the four
  `as unknown as { ... }` casts with a single Object.assign.

End-to-end verified: MCP handshake still returns tool "consult" under
server name "advisor"; disabled path returns the friendly textResult
text; whitespace context is rejected with the refine message.

author: rokkoo
body:
## Summary
- Restored legacy suggestion behavior for `Mailcheck.defaultDomains` in the `test@gml.com` regression case.
- Added regression coverage to ensure default domains prefer `gmail.com` over `msn.com` for `gml.com`.
- Scoped the legacy tie-break to `Mailcheck.defaultDomains` only, so custom domain arrays still use the normal `sift4` tie-breaking behavior.
## Details
`@opositatest/mailcheck@2.0.0` switched the default distance algorithm from `sift3` to `sift4`.  
That introduced a functional regression compared to `mailcheck@1.1.1`:
```js
Mailcheck.suggest(
  'test@gml.com',
  Mailcheck.defaultDomains,
  Mailcheck.defaultSecondLevelDomains,
  Mailcheck.defaultTopLevelDomains
);
```
Previous behavior:
test@gmail.com

Current behavior before this fix:
test@msn.com

The root cause was not only the algorithm change itself, but the interaction between:
- sift4 producing a tie between gmail.com and msn.com for gml.com
- findClosestDomain keeping the first minimum-distance match
- msn.com appearing before gmail.com in Mailcheck.defaultDomains
Fix
- Kept sift4 as the primary matching algorithm.
- Reintroduced sift3Distance only as a legacy tie-breaker when:

author: copilot
body:
Refactors the agentic command/event handler adapters to resolve the `Agent` at runtime from `AgentPlatform` using the aggregate name, with a `DefaultAgent` fallback when no matching agent is deployed. This reduces startup-time coupling to Spring bean naming and enables dynamic agent deployments.

## Changes Made

- Updated `AgenticCommandHandlerFunctionAdapter` and `AgenticEventHandlerFunctionAdapter` to take `aggregateName` and resolve the agent lazily (exact match or `{name}Agent` suffix match), with `DefaultAgent` fallback when no name match is found.
- Removed eager `Agent` bean lookup from `AgenticAggregateRuntimeFactory` and passed aggregate name into adapters instead.
- Removed `Autonomy.chooseAndAccomplishGoal()` fallback — it blocks the thread until completion, causing Kafka consumer timeouts with the tick() approach. Replaced with non-blocking default agent selection.
- `resolveAgentByName` now returns `Agent` directly (not `Optional<Agent>`), throwing `IllegalStateException` when the `DefaultAgent` is not deployed on the platform.
- Added `DefaultAgent` class in `org.elasticsoftware.akces.agentic.embabel` package, annotated with `@Agent(name = "DefaultAgent", planner = PlannerType.UTILITY)`. Exposes a `public static final String AGENT_NAME` constant used by both adapters to locate the fallback agent by name. This agent is always present on the `AgentPlatform` via Embabel's Spring component scanning.
- Both adapters' `resolveAgentByName` explicitly look for an agent named `DefaultAgent.AGENT_NAME` as the fallback, rather than using the first available agent from the platform.
- Added unit tests covering agent resolution scenarios (exact match, suffix match, default fallback, no-DefaultAgent-deployed error, no-agents-deployed error).
- Fixed javadoc in `AgenticAggregateRuntimeFactory` — removed stale `{@link Agent}` references that broke `javadoc:jar`.

### Motivation
- Improve Planet3D visual fidelity and interaction quality while keeping existing lifecycle contracts intact.
- Reduce unnecessary rendering cost and device-pixel overcommit by capping DPR and lowering expensive geometry detail.

author: degenmouse
body:
## Fix sandbox branch race condition and verify agent checkout

This PR addresses a race condition in the sandbox environment where the branch checkout performed during sandbox setup could complete before a concurrent `git fetch` finished, leaving the agent on the wrong branch. By adding an explicit `git fetch` + `git checkout` at agent server startup — before any messages are processed — we guarantee the server is always on the correct `SANDBOX_BRANCH` when it begins handling requests. The comment wording is also tightened to reflect that the branch restriction is now enforced more strictly ("must stay on" rather than "may only push to").

The `src/app/page.tsx` change replaces the styled hero headline ("Workflows that run themselves", including its highlight underline decoration) with a plain "Hello Mihai" string. This appears to be a temporary test edit, likely made by the agent during sandbox validation to confirm it could successfully modify and commit a file — it should be reverted before merging to production.

author: copilot
body:
The inference engine produced incoherent output due to a stateless SSM stub, wrong RoPE position tensor shape, and incorrect MoE expert weight renormalization. This PR replaces the stub with a correct DeltaNet implementation and fixes the other two bugs.

## SSM layer: full DeltaNet with persistent state (`build_ssm_layer`)

Previously a no-op silu+view approximation. Now implements the complete pipeline per `llama.cpp/qwen35moe.cpp`:

```
normed → attn_qkv → conv1d (sliding window) → silu → split Q/K/V
       → L2-norm Q/K → GQA expand (16→32 heads)
       → DeltaNet update: S_new = exp(gate_a)·S + β·outer(v - S@k, k)
       → output = S_new @ q
       → gated RMSNorm(output, ssm_norm) × silu(z) → ssm_out projection
```

### New persistent state per SSM layer
- **`SSMState.state`**: `[head_v_dim² , num_v_heads]` = `[16384, 32]` F32 — DeltaNet recurrent matrix
- **`SSMState.conv_buf`**: `[conv_kernel-1, conv_channels]` = `[3, 8192]` F32 — conv1d sliding window (ne[0]=3 is the fastest-varying conv-position axis)
- Allocated zero-initialized in `alloc_ssm_states()`, freed in destructor (same lifecycle as KV cache)

### Memory optimization
Uses `ggml_mul` broadcasting (`ggml_can_repeat(b, a)`) instead of `ggml_repeat` for per-head scalars, avoiding 4 × 2 MB temporaries per SSM layer (~240 MB saved across 30 layers):
```cpp
// gate_a [1,1,32] broadcasts to [128,128,32] — no explicit repeat needed
struct ggml_tensor* S_decayed = ggml_mul(ctx, S, eg_3d);
```

## Attention layer: fix RoPE position tensor shape

`ggml_rope_ext` expects `positions` of shape `[n_tokens]`, not `[n_heads]`:
```cpp
// Before: n_q_heads elements, one per head (wrong)
// After:
struct ggml_tensor* pos_t = ggml_new_tensor_1d(ctx, GGML_TYPE_I32, 1);
((int32_t*)pos_t->data)[0] = pos;
```

## MoE FFN: remove top-k weight renormalization

The reference does not renormalize after top-k selection; softmax probabilities are used directly as expert weights. The renormalization block (`wsum / wsum_bc`) has been removed.

## Infrastructure
- `build_graph` now tracks `ssm_ord` alongside `attn_ord` and passes both `gf` and `ssm_ord` to `build_ssm_layer`
- Compute buffer increased 256 MB → 512 MB to accommodate SSM intermediate tensors

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>


## Problem

The current inference implementation produces incoherent (irrelevant) output because several critical components are wrong or missing. The reference implementation is https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/src/models/qwen35moe.cpp

---

## Fixes Required

### Fix 1: `pipeline/inference.hpp` — Add SSM recurrent state cache

The SSM layers (DeltaNet) require a **per-layer recurrent state** that persists across tokens, similar to how attention layers have a KV cache. Add a `SSMState` struct and `ssm_states_` vector.

**Model dimensions for this GGUF:**
- `num_v_heads` = `time_step_rank` = 32 (from config `qwen35moe.ssm.time_step_rank`)
- `head_v_dim` = `inner_size / num_v_heads` = 4096 / 32 = 128
- `num_k_heads` = `group_count` = 16 (from config `qwen35moe.ssm.group_count`)
- `head_k_dim` = `state_size` = 128 (from config `qwen35moe.ssm.state_size`)
- State shape per SSM layer: `[head_v_dim * head_v_dim, num_v_heads]` = `[128*128, 32]` = `[16384, 32]`
  (This is the DeltaNet state: for each v-head, a `head_v_dim × head_v_dim` matrix)
- Conv state shape: `[conv_kernel-1, conv_channels]` = `[3, inner_size + 2*num_k_heads*head_k_dim]` = `[3, 4096 + 2*16*128]` = `[3, 8192]`

Add to `Qwen35moeInference` private section:
```cpp
struct SSMState {
    struct ggml_context* ctx      = nullptr;
    struct ggml_tensor*  state    = nullptr;  // [head_v_dim*head_v_dim, num_v_heads] F32  (DeltaNet recurrent state)
    struct ggml_tensor*  conv_buf = nullptr;  // [conv_kernel-1, conv_channels] F32  (conv1d sliding window)
};
std::vector<SSMState> ssm_states_;  // indexed by SSM layer ordinal (0..29)

void  free_ssm_states();
bool  alloc_ssm_states();
```

Also update `build_ssm_layer` signature to take `ggml_cgraph* gf` and `int ssm_ord`:
```cpp
struct ggml_tensor* build_ssm_layer(struct ggml_context* ctx,
                                    struct ggml_cgraph*  gf,
                                    struct ggml_tensor*  cur,
                                    int                  layer_idx,
                                    int                  ssm_ord);
```

---

### Fix 2: `pipeline/inference.cpp` — Complete rewrite of `build_ssm_layer`

Replace the current stub with a proper DeltaNet implementation following llama.cpp's `build_layer_attn_linear`.

**Parameters (from GGUF metadata):**
- `embed_dim` = 2048
- `inner_size` (`d_inner`) = 4096
- `num_v_heads` (`ssm_dt_rank`) = 32
- `head_v_dim` = 128
- `num_k_heads` (`group_count`) = 16
- `head_k_dim` (`state_size`) = 128
- `conv_kernel` = 4, so `conv_kernel_size - 1` = 3
- `conv_channels` = `inner_size + 2 * num_k_heads * head_k_dim` = `4096 + 2*16*128` = `8192`

**Algorithm:**
```
1. qkv_mixed = attn_qkv @ normed                          → [8192]
2. z         = attn_gate @ normed                          → [4096]

3. beta  = ssm_beta @ normed → sigmoid                    → [num_v_heads=32]  (reshape to [1, num_v_heads])
4. alpha = ssm_alpha @ normed                              → [num_v_heads=32]
5. alpha_biased   = alpha + ssm_dt_b
6. alpha_softplus = softplus(alpha_biased)
7. gate_a = alpha_softplus * ssm_a  → neg                 → [num_v_heads]  (reshape to [1, num_v_heads])
   Note: ssm_a values are negative in the model (they represent -A_log.exp())
   gate_a = -ggml_abs(gate_a)   or just: gate_a = ggml_neg(ggml_abs(gate_a))

8. Conv1d with sliding window state:
   - conv_buf = ssm_states_[ssm_ord].conv_buf              → [3, 8192]
   - concat(conv_buf, qkv_mixed_row)                       → [4, 8192]  (qkv_mixed as row)
   - conv_output = ggml_ssm_conv(concat, ssm_conv1d)       → [8192]
   - Update conv_buf: copy last 3 rows of concat back to ssm_states_[ssm_ord].conv_buf
   - conv_silu = silu(conv_output)                         → [8192]

9. Split conv_silu into q_conv, k_conv, v_conv:
   - q_conv: first  [head_k_dim * num_k_heads] = [2048] elements  → reshape [head_k_dim, num_k_heads]
   - k_conv: next   [head_k_dim * num_k_heads] = [2048] elements  → reshape [head_k_dim, num_k_heads]
   - v_conv: last   [head_v_dim * num_v_heads] = [4096] elements  → reshape [head_v_dim, num_v_heads]
   Total: 2048 + 2048 + 4096 = 8192 ✓

10. L2-normalize q_conv and k_conv per head (ggml_l2_norm on the head_k_dim dimension)

11. Expand k/q heads to match v heads if num_k_heads != num_v_heads:
    Repeat q_conv and k_conv along head axis: [head_k_dim, num_v_heads]

12. DeltaNet recurrent update (per v-head, for single token):
    state = ssm_states_[ssm_ord].state  → [head_v_dim*head_v_dim, num_v_heads]
    reshape state to [head_v_dim, head_v_dim, num_v_heads]
    
    For each head h (or using batched ggml ops):
      k_h = k_conv[:, h]  shape [head_k_dim] (= [head_v_dim] after expansion)
      q_h = q_conv[:, h]  shape [head_v_dim]
      v_h = v_conv[:, h]  shape [head_v_dim]
      S_h = state[:, :, h]  shape [head_v_dim, head_v_dim]
      
      # Delta rule update:
      beta_h = beta[h]   (scalar)
      gate_h = gate_a[h] (scalar, negative)
      
...

</details>

### What does this PR do?

author: llbartekll
body:
## Issue being fixed or feature implemented

  dashwallet-ios is migrating from DashSync to SwiftDashSDK. The backup seed phrase display (Settings → View Recovery Phrase) needs to read the 12-word mnemonic
  from SwiftDashSDK instead of DashSync. Today WalletStorage only stores the post-PBKDF2 64-byte seed via storeSeed, which is one-way — you cannot recover the
  human-readable words from it. This PR adds the missing mnemonic storage capability.
                                                                                                                                                                    
  ## What was done?
                                                                                                                                                                    
  Added three public methods to WalletStorage:              
  - storeMnemonic(_ mnemonic: String) — stores the BIP39 phrase as UTF-8 in iOS keychain at account wallet.mnemonic under the existing org.dash.wallet service.
  Idempotent (delete-before-add).                                                                                                                              
  - retrieveMnemonic() -> String — reads the mnemonic back. Throws WalletStorageError.mnemonicNotFound if absent.
  - deleteMnemonic() — removes the entry. Idempotent (accepts errSecItemNotFound).                               
                                                                                                                                                                    
  ## Added WalletStorageError.mnemonicNotFound enum case.
                                                                                                                                                                    
  Storage uses plain keychain with kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly — no PIN-derived encryption. This is parity with how DashSync stores mnemonics      
  (plaintext in keychain with OS-level protection). iOS keychain is hardware-backed (Secure Enclave), encrypted at rest, device-locked, and never backed up to      
  iCloud. Adding PIN encryption on top provides marginal value given a 4-digit PIN is brute-forceable in seconds at 10k PBKDF2 iterations.                          
                                                                                                                                                                    
  ## How Has This Been Tested?                                 
                                                                                                                                                                    
  - dashwallet-ios dashwallet scheme builds successfully with the updated package (local SPM reference)
  - dashwallet-ios dashpay scheme builds successfully                                                                                                               
  - The consumer side (dashwallet-ios) exercises storeMnemonic during wallet creation/migration/backfill and retrieveMnemonic during backup phrase display. Runtime
  testing deferred to a device that doesn't hit the known [DSChain retrieveWallets] host-app crash on iPhone 17 + iOS 26.3.                                         
                                                            
  ## Breaking Changes                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                    
  None. Additive only — three new public methods and one new error case. No existing API signatures changed.

author: nmstate-ai[bot]
body:
**Is this a BUG FIX or a FEATURE ?**:

/kind bug

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

The handler liveness probe runs `nmstatectl show` which outputs the full network state (~83KB). Kubernetes exec probes have a 10KB output buffer limit, causing "short write" errors in kubelet logs:

```
E0409 03:20:08.967146 7240 prober.go:256] "Unable to write all bytes from execInContainer" err="short write" expectedBytes=83397 actualBytes=10240
```

This PR changes the liveness probe command from `nmstatectl show` to `nmstatectl show lo`, which queries only the loopback interface (~685 bytes of output). The loopback interface is always present on every node, making it a reliable liveness check target while staying well within the 10KB limit.

Fixes #1476

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

The fix applies to both the default and debug (`-vv`) liveness probe variants.

**Release note**:

```release-note
Fix handler liveness probe "short write" errors by limiting nmstatectl output to the loopback interface only
```

author: akifarhan
body:
## Problem

On Android devices that still trigger the legacy `com.google.android.c2dm.intent.RECEIVE` broadcast (older Android versions and certain OEM builds), Intercom push notifications are displayed **twice**.

## Root Cause

The merged Android manifest ends up with two simultaneous Intercom push handlers:

| Handler | Registered by | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| `io.maido.intercom.PushInterceptReceiver` | `intercom_flutter` plugin manifest | `com.google.android.c2dm.intent.RECEIVE` (legacy C2DM broadcast) |
| `io.intercom.android.sdk.fcm.IntercomFcmMessengerService` | `intercom-sdk-fcm` AAR (transitive dep of `intercom-sdk`) | `com.google.firebase.MESSAGING_EVENT` (modern Firebase path) |

On affected devices, both handlers receive the same push payload and independently call `handlePush()`, resulting in two notifications being displayed.

`IntercomFcmMessengerService` is included automatically as a transitive dependency whenever `intercom-sdk` is used — meaning both handlers are always present when `initSdk()` is called in the Application class per the recommended setup.

## Fix

Remove `PushInterceptReceiver` from the plugin's `AndroidManifest.xml`. `IntercomFcmMessengerService` (registered by the native SDK's own AAR) is the intended modern handler and covers all cases including background and killed-state delivery when `initSdk()` is called in the Application class.

**Removed from `android/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`:**

```xml
<receiver
    android:name="io.maido.intercom.PushInterceptReceiver"
    android:exported="true"
    android:permission="com.google.android.c2dm.permission.SEND">
    <intent-filter>
        <action android:name="com.google.android.c2dm.intent.RECEIVE" />
    </intent-filter>
</receiver>
```

`PushInterceptReceiver.kt` can also be removed entirely as it becomes unreachable.

## Testing

Tested on an affected device (OEM build still triggering the C2DM broadcast):
- Before fix: every Intercom push notification displayed twice
- After fix: single notification displayed correctly
- Background and killed-state push delivery unaffected

author: stackbilt-admin
body:
## Summary

Adds the **outbound** side of the security policy — rules for when Stackbilt itself (operators and internal agents) files findings against our own public repositories. The existing policy only covered **inbound** reports from external researchers; this closes the gap.

This PR introduces the full framework: policy text, a machine-readable public repo manifest, a canonical per-repo SECURITY.md template, and an updated ecosystem doc that documents the OSS Core / Commercial Extension pattern without leaking private repo names.

## What's in this PR

### 1. `src/content/docs/security.md` — new "Outbound Disclosure" section

- **Severity → channel routing matrix** for public vs private repos
- **Neutral-filer rule** — no internal agent branding, no session footers, no implication of internal AI review capability
- **Reference framing rules** — cite RFCs, OWASP, Cloudflare public docs; never internal CLAUDE.md, memory stores, or private repo commits
- **Scrub list** — classes of identifier that must not appear in public artifacts
- **Cross-repo chain rule** — never publicly describe a finding that chains with a private-repo bug
- **Approval gate** — autonomous agents may file against private repos without approval but must get operator approval before filing against public repos
- **Disclosure audit log** — persistent trail of every filing action by internal agents
- **Policy Authoring Rule** — the policy itself must pass its own scrub filter during revisions; includes a case study of the near-miss that produced this section (see "The Meta-Finding" below)
- Primary reporting email flipped from `security@` to `admin@stackbilt.dev`
- GitHub Security Advisory added as per-repo preferred channel for critical/high disclosures

### 2. `src/content/docs/ecosystem.md` — two new sections

- **Open Source Libraries** — table of all 14 public OSS repos under Stackbilt-dev with one-line purposes, repo links, and npm package names where applicable. These are libraries that were "silently public" — shipped, visible on GitHub, but not narrated anywhere in the docs. Now they have canonical documentation.
- **OSS Core ↔ Commercial Extension Pattern** — documents the dual-repo structure where a public OSS core (e.g., `aegis-oss`) has commercial productization built on top. Names only the OSS core; describes commercial extensions abstractly without naming them. Enforces the moat-protecting convention that public discussion always references the OSS repo.
- Service Map AEGIS row updated to point at `aegis-oss` (removes the "Internal cognitive agent" phrasing that directly contradicted the new OSS Libraries section)

### 3. `public/ecosystem/repo-visibility.json` — new machine-readable manifest

Served at `docs.stackbilt.dev/ecosystem/repo-visibility.json` for agent pre-flight lookups.

- **Public allowlist only** — 16 repos, each with `ecosystem_role`, `disclosure_channel`, and `fallback_channel`
- **`default_policy` stanza** — any Stackbilt-dev repository not listed here is treated as private by default; unlisted repos must not be referenced in public
- **Routing matrix** — severity → channel decisions
- **Reference framing allowlist / prohibition list** — machine-readable version of the policy's citation rules
- **`agent_consumers` section** documenting how internal automation consumes this file at pre-flight

**⚠️ Contains NO private repo names.** Private-name scrub lists are generated dynamically by agents at session start via the authenticated GitHub API (\`gh api orgs/Stackbilt-dev/repos --paginate\`). The scrub list is held in memory only, never persisted to a public-visible location. This design prevents the manifest itself from becoming a repo-enumeration attack surface.

### 4. `public/ecosystem/SECURITY.md.template` — canonical per-repo SECURITY.md

One-file-fits-all template for per-repository SECURITY.md files across the entire Stackbilt-dev organization. Placeholder \`{{REPO_NAME}}\` is replaced at rollout time. Points at \`admin@stackbilt.dev\` and the canonical policy URL.

This unblocks a follow-up rollout that will apply the template to every repo (public and private) so every repo has a standardized security reporting entry point.

## The Meta-Finding — why this PR has a "Policy Authoring Rule" section

**The first draft of this policy would have shipped the exact leak it was designed to prevent.**

The initial `repo-visibility.json` I wrote listed every Stackbilt-dev repository by name — public AND private — because the natural instinct when documenting a visibility manifest is to be thorough. Publishing that file at `docs.stackbilt.dev/ecosystem/repo-visibility.json` would have converted "private repos exist but are not externally enumerable" into "here is the complete roster of every internal Stackbilt project." Private repo names are not currently discoverable via unauthenticated \`gh api\` calls, so the manifest would have been a pure reconnaissance gift.

The initial ecosystem.md dual-repo section also named private commercial extensions directly in a table alongside their OSS cores. Same class of leak, narrower scope.

Both were caught in a pre-commit review pass before anything was pushed. **No disclosure occurred.** But the near-miss validates the rule: policy documents must be authored with the policy's own scrub rules applied from the start, not written thoroughly and scrubbed after. The highest-risk context for accidental disclosure is the policy authoring context itself, because the author has the most private context loaded at exactly the moment they're writing public-facing text.

This is codified in the new **Policy Authoring Rule** section with the above near-miss as the case study.

## Known pre-existing scrub gaps NOT addressed in this PR

These were present in ecosystem.md before this PR and are editorial decisions about how the deployed auth and service-binding architecture is described. Fixing them requires broader rewriting of those sections and is out of scope for this policy introduction. Tracked as a follow-up issue:

- Service Map line 29: \`tarotscript-worker\` service binding identifier
- Service Map line 30: \`img-forge-gateway\` service binding identifier
- Authentication section lines 123, 129: \`edge-auth\` named by private repo name

A follow-up issue on this repo will track the scrub pass and propose the replacement wording.

## Test plan

- [x] \`npm run build\` passes (pre-commit hook verified, 9 pages built in 18.97s)
- [x] No private repo names appear in committed files (grep-verified against full private repo list)
- [x] \`repo-visibility.json\` validates as JSON
- [x] Cross-reference check: all 16 public repos in the manifest match \`gh api orgs/Stackbilt-dev/repos --jq '.[] | select(.private == false and .archived == false) | .name'\`
- [ ] Manual review of policy wording for tone + actionability
- [ ] Confirm the \`{{REPO_NAME}}\` placeholder substitution strategy for the SECURITY.md rollout
- [ ] Confirm \`admin@stackbilt.dev\` is the intended canonical address (security@ is demoted)

## Follow-up work unlocked by this PR

1. File a follow-up issue on this repo to track the pre-existing scrub gaps (\`tarotscript-worker\`, \`img-forge-gateway\`, \`edge-auth\` in ecosystem.md)
2. Roll out the canonical SECURITY.md template to every repo in Stackbilt-dev (54 repos, batched in parallel, one small PR per repo)
3. Implement the CodeBeast pre-flight filter spec per the new policy (separate internal issue)
4. Staged Charter CLI adoption across all Node repos (separate workstream, blocked on this PR + SECURITY.md rollout)

`rnef` was renamed to `rockjs`. The old `@rnef/plugin-repack` doesn't pass `reactNativePath` to repack's start command, which repack 5.2.5 now requires via `getDevMiddleware(cliConfig.reactNativePath)`. This causes all dev servers to crash. `@rock-js/plugin-repack@0.13.0` includes the fix.

## 📝 What changed

- Replaced `@rnef/cli` with `rock` and `@rnef/*` with `@rock-js/*` at `^0.13.0` across all 5 repack apps
- Renamed `rnef.config.mjs` → `rock.config.mjs` with updated imports
- Updated all native build files (Podfile, settings.gradle, build.gradle, project.pbxproj) to reference `rock` instead of `rnef`
- Updated CI scripts and workflows (`RNEF_PATH` → `ROCK_PATH`, `rnef-build-extra-params` → `rock-build-extra-params`)
- Updated rspack config comments (`rnef start/bundle` → `rock start/bundle`)
- Updated `packages/mobile-sdk/lib/devDependencies.json`
- Added `.rock` to `.gitignore` (kept `.rnef` for safety)
- Regenerated `pnpm-lock.yaml`

## 🧪 How to test

1. `pnpm install` in `frameworks/react-native-repack`
2. `pnpm -r run check-deps` — all aligned
3. Start a dev server: `cd apps/mobile-host && pnpm start` — should not crash

## Summary

Claude Code (the MCP host) auto-parses JSON-looking string arguments into `dict`/`list` before passing them to MCP tools. Tool functions that declared their JSON-shaped parameters as `str | None` rejected those calls with a Pydantic validation error before the CLI was even invoked:

\`\`\`
Input should be a valid string [type=string_type, input_value={'TextAd': {'Title': '...'}}, input_type=dict]
\`\`\`

This PR widens the type of every JSON-shaped parameter to accept `str | dict` (or `str | list` for `sitelinks_add`, which expects a JSON array) and serializes back to a string with `json.dumps` before forwarding to \`direct-cli\`. The CLI invocation is unchanged on the wire — recorded cassettes still match.

quic_dist:stop_accepting(Node) -> ok

Align `sentry-task-enqueued-time` format with sentry-python by storing epoch seconds in the producer interceptor and computing `messaging.message.receive.latency` from seconds in the consumer interceptor.

body:
## Summary

This PR introduces a complete Twitter-to-Feishu daily scheduling system that automatically searches Twitter/X for specified topics, summarizes results using LLM, and sends formatted reports to Feishu via webhook.

## Key Changes

- **New Scheduler Engine** (`twitter_feishu_scheduler.py`): Core async scheduler that runs jobs at specified Beijing time (cron-based), manages lifecycle (start/stop/run_now), and maintains execution history
  
- **Job Executor** (`twitter_feishu_job.py`): Orchestrates the complete pipeline:
  - Searches multiple Twitter targets in parallel
  - Generates LLM-powered summaries with fallback to raw data
  - Sends formatted Markdown reports to Feishu
  - Tracks execution metrics (tweets found, duration, status)

- **LLM Prompt Templates** (`twitter_feishu_prompt.py`): Structured prompts for generating professional daily reports with sections for overview, detailed summaries, key signals, and trending accounts

- **Data Models** (`twitter_feishu_models.py`): Pydantic models for configuration, execution records, and scheduler state with validation

- **Tool Integration** (`twitter_feishu_tools.py`): Creates a Tool interface supporting `start`, `stop`, `run_now`, and `status` actions for agent control

- **Conditional Registration** (`twitter_feishu_register.py`): Registers the scheduler only when both Feishu webhook and Twitter credentials are configured; builds search, LLM, and Feishu callback functions

- **Comprehensive Tests** (`test_twitter_feishu_scheduler.py`): 40+ unit tests covering models, prompts, job execution, scheduler lifecycle, error handling, and tool operations

- **Configuration**: Added environment variables for cron schedule and search targets JSON in `.env.example`

## Notable Implementation Details

- **Beijing Timezone Aware**: All scheduling calculations use Beijing timezone (UTC+8) for consistent daily execution
- **Graceful Degradation**: Works without LLM (falls back to raw data), handles search failures per-target without stopping entire job
- **Execution History**: Maintains last 50 execution records with metrics for monitoring
- **Async-First**: Fully async implementation with proper task cancellation and error handling
- **Flexible Search Targets**: Supports multiple Twitter search queries with configurable result limits and time windows

author: copilot
body:
Refactors the monolithic filesystem-backed game into the specified three-layer architecture: engine core (本体层), virtual filesystem interface (接口层), and persistence (持久化层). The key design shift: game state lives in memory, and the filesystem is a presentation layer — not the source of truth.

### Architecture

- **`src/engine/`** — In-memory world state: entities, player, areas, combat, farming. `World` struct is the single source of truth. Entities use a generic `EntityId` + `HashMap<String, Value>` property bag.
- **`src/vfs/`** — Virtual filesystem built on-the-fly from engine state. Directories = areas, files = entity interfaces, `/proc/{status,areas,help}` = system views. No real filesystem backing.
- **`src/command/`** — Command parser and executor. Commands operate on VFS, which translates to engine mutations. Hierarchy: basic (`ls/cd/pwd`), info (`cat/find`), ops (`cp/mv/rm`), extended (`attack/talk/use`), system (`save/help/quit`).
- **`src/persistence/`** — Config loading from `world/config/*.yaml`, save/load via single `world/save.yaml` snapshot.

### What changed

- Removed `notify` filesystem watcher, `serde_json`, `unicode-width` dependencies
- Removed `actions.rs`, `world.rs`, `template.rs`, `ui_template.rs`, `exploration.rs` (old monolithic modules)
- Game loop now uses a Linux-style prompt (`player@area /path $`) instead of menu-driven UI
- `attack <target>` / `talk <npc>` / `use <item>` replace the old menu-based combat/interaction

### Example session

```
hero@森林 /森林 $ ls
.info  哥布林(Lv1)  狼(Lv1)  老者  草药

hero@森林 /森林 $ cat .info
名称: 森林
描述: 宁静的树林，适合新手探索。

hero@森林 /森林 $ attack 哥布林
⚔  hero (HP:100/100)  vs  哥布林(Lv1) (HP:30/30)
...
胜利！获得 25 经验和 8 金币。

hero@森林 /森林 $ cat /proc/status
=== 玩家状态 ===
名称: hero
HP: 95/100
等级: 1
```

## Summary

This PR adds comprehensive specification, planning, and task documentation for two major features in the E07 sensor data pipeline:

- **#117 (REP Sensor Import)**: Parsing `;SENSOR:`, `;SENSOR2:`, `;SENSOR3:`, and `;SENSORARC` lines from REP files and embedding sensor contacts into track features
- **#118 (Sensor Rendering)**: Leaflet custom canvas layer for rendering bearing lines, ambiguous bearings, sensor arcs, and snail mode fading on the map

## Key Changes

### REP Sensor Import (#117)
- **spec.md**: User scenarios for parsing all four sensor line formats (v1/v2/v3 and arcs), with acceptance criteria for contact embedding, ambiguous bearing support, and frequency data
- **plan.md**: Implementation strategy covering Python service module development, pytest test suite, and performance targets (10k lines in <1s)
- **data-model.md**: Schema definitions for `ParsedSensorContact` (intermediate) and output `SensorContact` dicts conforming to LinkML schema

## Summary

Widens the `errlog` parameter type on `stdio_client()` and the platform-specific process helpers to accept `int` in addition to `TextIO`. This allows callers to pass `subprocess.DEVNULL`, `subprocess.PIPE`, or other integer file descriptor constants that `subprocess.Popen` and `anyio.open_process` already support.

Previously, suppressing stderr from a child process required a `type: ignore` comment or wrapping `subprocess.DEVNULL` — even though the underlying APIs already accept it.

## Changes

- `stdio_client()`: `errlog: TextIO` → `errlog: TextIO | int`
- `_create_platform_compatible_process()`: same
- `create_windows_process()`: `errlog: TextIO | None` → `errlog: TextIO | int | None`
- `_create_windows_fallback_process()`: same
- Added `test_stdio_client_devnull_errlog` regression test

## Test plan

- New test spawns a process with `errlog=subprocess.DEVNULL`, verifies it starts and communicates correctly via stdin/stdout
- Existing tests continue to pass (default `sys.stderr` behavior unchanged)

Closes #1806

author: aldoborrero
body:
## Summary

`buildGoApplication { goProxy = "..."; }` reached the eval-time `go list` (via `resolveGoPackages`) but not the per-module fetch FODs — those only saw `GOPROXY` via `impureEnvVars`. Under daemon nix or remote builders the daemon's environment has no `GOPROXY`, so the FOD's `go mod download` fell back to Go's default `proxy.golang.org,direct` and private modules became unfetchable (no `git` in `nativeBuildInputs` either, so `direct` can't help).

`fetchGoModule` now accepts a per-call `goProxy` and exports it at the top of `buildPhase`. The export is prepended via `lib.optionalString` so when `goProxy` is null (the default) `buildPhase` is byte-identical and existing `.drv` paths don't change.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/nix/fetch_go_module_test.nix`: default `buildPhase` has no `GOPROXY`; with `goProxy` set, `export GOPROXY=...` appears
- [x] `nix-instantiate tests/fixtures/testify-basic/dag.nix` produces the same `.drv` path as `origin/main` (hash-neutral when `goProxy=null`)
- [x] `nix flake check` (formatting)

_Work in progress..._

# Update 1

### Static generation and route approach

The first step is to generate a safe and long-lasting approach to consuming content for specifically `supabase-js@latest` route (`/reference/javascript`). We want to generate a new .mdx file ahead-of-build within `/content/reference`  plus a .json file for navigation sections. This is important because it will allow us to use generate markdown for both potential vectorized search using Markdown pragma plus generating .md files for Agents and AI Tooling.

After some investigation on how we handle these routes and Next.js possibilities, the ideal scenario is to, in the future, use a `layout.tsx` file under the `reference/[library]/[version]` path. Next.js passes a `params` Promise resolving to an object with both library and version which we can use to fetch the static Markdown already generated. But this is only possible when all reference routes are generated like this. In the meantime we are patching.

### Adapter and parsing script

I tried several iterations using agents to generate an equivalent from what we have (at least close), and it got surprisingly close. But things will get more complicated when we have to resolve AST elements to custom MDX components we hold in our codebase. Initially we are consuming the `combined.json` file but some information is missing. Still we want the tsdoc output to be the main driver of the generated information on page to create a clear definition of the page structure so it solely depends on it, and then it can be aggregated via partials or another reconciliation method for extra markdown content. We will consult the SDK team further for this.

### Motivation
- Prevent SSRF and internal network probing by validating and normalizing user-provided scan URLs before launching Playwright. 
- Eliminate resource leaks from Playwright `browser/context/page` on exceptions to keep the scan worker pool healthy. 
- Protect request workers from vendor LLM stalls by applying hard timeouts and make AI response parsing more defensive. 
- Improve DB read performance for history/detail endpoints with targeted Prisma indexes.

### Description
- Added `backend/src/utils/urlSafety.js` to validate URLs (scheme, hostname, credential stripping), DNS-resolve hosts, and block localhost and private/internal IP ranges. 
- Updated `backend/src/controllers/scanController.js` to use the URL validator, normalize the safe URL, tighten input checks, validate scan id parsing, and keep SSE/JSON pipeline behavior consistent. 
- Refactored `backend/src/services/scanService.js` to always close `page`, `context`, and `browser` in a `finally` block and to use safer load/wait sequencing to reduce flakiness and leaks. 
- Strengthened AI adapter layer in `backend/src/services/ai/aiProvider.js` by normalizing/parsing AI fixes with size caps and expected-count padding and by exporting a `withTimeout` helper; applied `withTimeout` to OpenAI, Claude, and Gemini provider calls to bound remote calls. 
- Added Prisma indexes in `backend/prisma/schema.prisma` for `Scan.createdAt`, `Violation.scanId`, `Violation.scanId+priorityScore`, and `Violation.ruleId` to optimize history and violation queries.
