author: lendtrain
body:
## Summary

Replaces the "~1.2% of loan amount" closing-cost heuristic with explicit directives to call the new `~~pricer calculate_closing_cost` MCP tool (added in [lendtrain/mortgage-pricer#136](https://github.com/lendtrain/mortgage-pricer/pull/136)) and use its `total` verbatim.

## Why this matters

On a UT $1,000,000 conventional refi:
- **Heuristic** (what the plugin currently returns): ~$12,020
- **Deterministic calculator**: **\$4,170.50**

That is 2.9x too high. Because closing costs drive 25-30% of the weighted refinance recommendation score (monthly savings 30-35%, breakeven 25-30%, rate improvement ~20%, interest saved ~10-15%), the heuristic can flip a correct \"refi now\" recommendation into \"don't bother\" or vice versa.

The bug was in four places, not just one:

1. **`plugins/mortgage/commands/refi-quote.md §3.2`** — the main refi-quote flow explicitly told the agent: *\"Refinance closing costs are typically around 1.2% of the loan amount... ALWAYS use the \`closing_cost_estimate_percent\` from \`mortgage.local.md\` (currently 1.2%) for the estimate.\"* This was the primary code path.
2. **`plugins/mortgage/skills/mortgage-loan-officer/SKILL.md §\"Estimated Closing Costs\"`** — had a fallback step: *\"If the \`closing-costs\` skill is unavailable or the state is not covered, fall back to \`closing_cost_estimate_percent\` from \`mortgage.local.md\` (default: 1.2%) as a rough estimate.\"*
3. **`plugins/mortgage/skills/mortgage-loan-officer/mortgage.local.md`** — held the config value `closing_cost_estimate_percent: 1.2` in YAML frontmatter and documented it in the body.
4. **`plugins/mortgage/skills/closing-costs/SKILL.md`** — instructed the agent to manually sum per-state reference fee schedules that drift from the pricer's canonical calculator (different settlement fees, different CPL amounts, different title insurance bracket formulas, missing Utah refi discount, etc.).

Even in the \"happy path\" where the agent used the closing-costs skill, the per-state tables in that skill were inconsistent with the pricer, so the borrower saw different numbers than what the pricing engine would compute. The only way to guarantee consistency is to make the pricer the single source of truth.

## What changed

### `plugins/mortgage/commands/refi-quote.md` (§3.2 Estimated Closing Costs)
- Replaces \"fall back to `closing_cost_estimate_percent`\" with an explicit `calculate_closing_cost` tool-call spec.
- Removes the presentation rule that defended *\"~1.2% of your loan amount\"* as reasonable borrower-facing copy.
- Adds an explicit **\"NEVER present as a percentage of loan\"** rule.
- On unsupported state, defers to `mortgage-compliance` instead of inventing a number.

### `plugins/mortgage/skills/mortgage-loan-officer/SKILL.md`
- **§\"Estimated Closing Costs\"** fully rewritten: tool-call spec with field mappings and response shape, explicit \"you MUST call this tool\" directive, unsupported-state fallback (defer to compliance), and guidance to use `response.total` verbatim.
- **§\"FHA Streamline Pricing Strategy\"** updated to reference the tool (`isStreamline: true`, `monthsSinceEndorsement`, `previousUfmipAmount`).
- **§\"Breakeven Period\"** updated with a note that `estimatedClosingCosts` comes from the tool, not a percentage heuristic, and a brief explanation of why (2-3x skew, 25-30% weight in the score).

### `plugins/mortgage/skills/mortgage-loan-officer/mortgage.local.md`
- Removes `closing_cost_estimate_percent: 1.2` from the YAML frontmatter.
- Replaces the \"Configuration Reference → closing_cost_estimate_percent\" body section with a note explaining why closing costs are NOT configured here and must come from the pricer tool.

### `plugins/mortgage/skills/closing-costs/SKILL.md`
- Reframes the skill as a **presentation guide**, not a calculation skill.
- Adds a new \"Data Source: `~~pricer calculate_closing_cost` MCP Tool\" section at the top with the tool-call spec, response shape, and field-to-table mapping.
- Rewrites \"Calculation Procedure\" as \"Presentation Procedure\" (uses tool response fields, not state tables).
- Adds a warning banner on \"State Fee Schedules\" marking them as historical reference only — NOT the source of truth for dollar amounts. Pricer values are canonical.
- Adds \"Rules\" bullet forbidding percentage-of-loan heuristics.

### `plugins/mortgage/skills/security-guardrails/SKILL.md`
- Removes `closing_cost_estimate_percent` from the list of protected threshold values (it no longer exists).

## Dependency on `lendtrain/mortgage-pricer#136`

This PR references the `~~pricer calculate_closing_cost` MCP tool, which is added in [lendtrain/mortgage-pricer#136](https://github.com/lendtrain/mortgage-pricer/pull/136). That PR must merge and deploy first — otherwise the tool call will fail and the skill's own unsupported-state fallback (defer to compliance) will kick in.

## Test plan

- [x] **Heuristic removal verified**: `grep -rn -i '1\\.2%|1\\.2 percent|closing_cost_estimate_percent|percent of (the )?loan' plugins/` returns only intentional *forbidding* directives, no remaining heuristic instructions. Specifically, the following files now contain ONLY directives forbidding the heuristic:
    - `plugins/mortgage/commands/refi-quote.md` (line 743, 772 — both forbid)
    - `plugins/mortgage/skills/mortgage-loan-officer/SKILL.md` (line 263, 334 — both forbid)
    - `plugins/mortgage/skills/mortgage-loan-officer/mortgage.local.md` (line 16 — forbids)
    - `plugins/mortgage/skills/closing-costs/SKILL.md` (lines 5, 565, 647 — all forbid)
- [x] **No stray 1.2% language**: the `closing_cost_estimate_percent` config key no longer exists in the YAML frontmatter of `mortgage.local.md`.
- [x] **Security guardrails consistent**: the key is also removed from the \"protected threshold values\" list in `security-guardrails/SKILL.md` so the agent doesn't claim to protect a key that no longer exists.
- [x] **Tool call specs are complete**: all three locations (refi-quote.md §3.2, mortgage-loan-officer SKILL.md §Estimated Closing Costs, closing-costs SKILL.md §Data Source) specify the same parameter names and types that match the pricer's `ClosingCostRequestSchema` from [lendtrain/mortgage-pricer#136](https://github.com/lendtrain/mortgage-pricer/pull/136).
- [ ] **Manual end-to-end once pricer PR is deployed**: run `/refi-quote` for a UT $1M conventional refinance scenario and confirm the quote returns `total = $4,170.50` (within rounding), not ~\$12,020. (Requires the pricer PR to be deployed to the Railway environment powering `~~pricer`.)

## Fixes / References

- Fixes lendtrain/mortgage#5 (bug 3)
- Related: lendtrain/mortgage-pricer#135 (bug 3)
- Depends on: lendtrain/mortgage-pricer#136

Bug:    
    The buff icon for healing with bandages expires too soon,

    then RemoveBuff at the end of EndHeal clears it immediately.

author: copilot
body:
The contact experience exposed a harvestable email address in page markup/metadata, and needed to remain easy for legitimate users to complete with browser autofill. This update reduces bot-visible email exposure while keeping the current client-side mailto flow intact.

- **Email exposure removed from static HTML/metadata**
  - Removed hardcoded recipient email from `contact.html` JSON-LD (`ContactPage` main entity).
  - Removed hardcoded recipient email from `index.html` JSON-LD (`EducationalOrganization`).
  - Updated the contact form notice to avoid rendering a literal email address.

- **Client-side mailto flow retained without static recipient leakage**
  - Kept form submission behavior (open prefilled email draft) but no longer stores the recipient as plain text in markup.
  - Recipient is assembled at submit time in JS and used to build the `mailto:` URL.

- **Autofill and anti-bot behavior refined**
  - Preserved user autofill on real user fields (`name`, `email`) and form-level autofill.
  - Kept a hidden honeypot field with neutral naming to reduce obvious bot heuristics while maintaining spam filtering behavior.
  - Added a neutral non-email form fallback action (`action="#"`) to avoid exposing recipient data in attributes.

```html
<form id="contact-form" action="#" aria-label="Contact form" autocomplete="on">
```

```js
var email = ['aspiece', 'geneseeisd.org'].join('@');
var mailtoUrl = 'mailto:' + email + '?subject=' + encodeURIComponent(subject) + '&body=' + encodeURIComponent(body);
window.location.href = mailtoUrl;
```

body:
Addresses all Lighthouse Accessibility and Performance audit failures on `https://akiprisaye-web.pages.dev/`. Covers missing ARIA names, invalid role usage, non-composited animations, and missing CSS minification.

---

## 🔧 ARIA / Accessibility

**Role & attribute fixes:**

- `BookingLinkBadge`, `SearchCompareHub`: click-triggered panels changed from `role="tooltip"` → `role="region"` with `aria-label` (tooltips are hover-only per ARIA spec)
- `PredictionBadge`, `AnomalyBadge`: tooltip elements get `id` + `aria-label`; triggers get `aria-describedby`
- `FeedbackWidget`: removed invalid `role="presentation"` from plain backdrop `<div>`
- `Header`: `aria-haspopup="true"` → `aria-haspopup="menu"`

**Dialog names:**
- Fixed duplicate `id="modal-title"` across two components → unique IDs (`signalement-modal-title`, `product-review-modal-title`)
- All `role="dialog"` elements now have `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`

**Tab/panel roles:**
- `TerritoryPriceChart`, `PriceEvolutionChart` tabpanels: added dynamic `aria-label`
- `ComprehensiveProductSheet` tablist: added `aria-label`

**Form inputs:**
- BarcodeScanner zoom `<input type="range">`: added `aria-label`, `aria-valuenow/min/max`
- BarcodeScanner manual EAN, Comparateur search, ProductPriceLookup submit button: added `aria-label`
- DomMapTimeline, NearbyDeals sliders: added `aria-label` + `aria-value*`
- FeedbackWidget textarea: proper `htmlFor`/`id` label association
- Messagerie chat textarea: added `aria-label`
- InflationPressureIndexCard progressbar: added `aria-label`
- `LanguageSelector` trigger button: added `aria-label={Langue : ${currentLang.name}}`
- 12 unlabeled `<select>` elements across pages: added French `aria-label`
- `select.jsx` / `ui/select.jsx` wrappers: spread `{...props}` to allow `aria-label` passthrough

---

## ⚡ Performance

**Composited animations** — all transitions now use only `transform` / `opacity` (GPU-composited, no layout/paint):

| Before | After | File |
|---|---|---|
| `width` transition on bars | `transform: scaleX()` | `home-v5.css` + 4 React components |
| `left` on mobile nav | `transform: translateX()` | `shared-nav.css` |
| `top` on skip-link | `transform: translateY()` | `a11y.css` |

| `background-position` shimmer | `transform: translateX()` | `animations.css` |
| `width` on nav underline | `transform: scaleX()` | `layout.css` |

**CSS minification:** added `cssMinify: true` to `vite.config.ts` (was implicit via Terser but now explicit and guaranteed).

---

### Motivation
- The governed gateway call path only blocked hard denials (`outcome == "HALT"`) and ignored Faramesh `DEFER` decisions (which arrive as `outcome == "ABSTAIN"` with `effect == "DEFER"`), allowing sensitive actions to execute without approval.
- The change aims to ensure deferred decisions trigger the approval flow instead of being bypassed.

### Description
- In `src/api/services/gateway_client.py` `call_gateway_method_governed` now treats `decision.effect == "DEFER"` the same as a denial and raises `GovernanceError` (the error reason message was adjusted to reflect deny/defer semantics).
- Added targeted regression tests in `tests/api/test_gateway_client.py` that assert a `DEFER`/`ABSTAIN` decision blocks execution and that a `PERMIT`/`EXECUTE` decision still allows the gateway call.
- The fix is minimal and scoped to governance enforcement prior to dispatching `call_gateway_method` so normal behavior for permitted calls is preserved.

### Testing
- Ran `pytest -q tests/api/test_gateway_client.py` which passed (`2 passed`).

author: dhruvarya-db
body:
The way DockerHub token is passed for logging in while publishing the rest-fixture image is not safe. See https://www.codegenes.net/blog/docker-using-password-via-the-cli-is-insecure-use-password-stdin/ . Command-line arguments like -p can be visible to other processes, increasing the risk of exposure. 

Instead of using -p, we use echo <token> | docker login ... --password-stdin for authentication now. This is the recommended way of doing it as per the official docker docs: https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/login/#password-stdin.

author: misut
body:
## Summary

Two small UX fixes that landed together because both touch the user's read of the docs page:

- **`layout::row` now defaults to `CrossAxisAlignment::Center`** so a `widget::text` next to a padded `widget::code` shares a centerline instead of leaving the shorter child dangling at the top of the row. This makes the inline pattern repeated through `docs/src/main.cpp:117-129` (the Components list) line up the way you'd expect — code-box monospace text and the plain description text now sit on the same baseline. With the line-cell height of `font_size * 1.6`, the cell midline lands near `font_size * 0.8`, which approximates the canvas `'top'`-baseline ascent, so centering also approximately baseline-aligns text-cells of similar font sizes (16 vs 14.4 here).
- **Hover cursor / `phenotype_set_hover` are now refreshed on scroll and resize.** Previously the cursor and `g_app.hovered_id` were only updated inside `pointermove`. Scrolling without moving the mouse left a `pointer` cursor stuck on whatever was last under the mouse, even after the button scrolled out of view. A new `applyHoverAt(clientX, clientY)` helper centralizes the hit-test + cursor + `phenotype_set_hover` logic and runs from `pointermove`, `pointerleave`, `wheel` and `resize`. The pointer position is cached as `lastClientX/Y` (reset to `-1` on `pointerleave` so off-canvas periods stay quiet).

## Test plan

- [x] `exon test` (native): existing 14 + new `row cross-align center default` regression test, all green
- [x] `exon test` with `-fsanitize=address,undefined`: clean
- [x] `exon test --target wasm32-wasi`: all green
- [x] `cd docs && exon build --target wasm32-wasi`: clean
- [x] `node --check shim/phenotype.js`: syntax OK
- [ ] Manual browser smoke tests post-merge:
  - Hover Counter +/- buttons → cursor becomes pointer
  - Scroll the buttons out of view without moving the mouse → cursor reverts to default
  - Scroll until a different button lands under the cursor → its hover background applies (proves `phenotype_set_hover` is also refreshed, not just CSS cursor)
  - Resize the window so layout reflows under a stationary pointer → cursor matches the new content
  - "Components" section: code box and adjacent text on each row look vertically aligned
  - Counter row's +/-/Reset buttons + footer's ` · ` link list: still visually OK with Center cross-align

## Notes

- The widget::code padding-16 sizing is unchanged — it's appropriate as a standalone block (e.g. the Quick Start fence in `docs/src/main.cpp:100`). A future PR can split inline_code vs code_block if the inline form needs tighter padding.
- Mixed font-sizes very different from each other (e.g. heading inline with small text) won't perfectly baseline-align with Center, only approximately. A real `CrossAxisAlignment::Baseline` mode is left for a follow-up if it ever matters.

body:
## Motivation

PR #22545 introduced the weekly `update_est_time.py` script that updates `est_time` values from CI data. However, it keyed timings by `(filename, backend)` instead of `(filename, suite)`. This caused files with multiple `register_cuda_ci` calls for different suites (e.g., H100 vs B200) to get the same `est_time` value for all suites.

For example, in PR #22550 (generated by the workflow), `test_gpt_oss_4gpu.py` got `est_time=304` for both `stage-c-test-4-gpu-h100` and `stage-c-test-4-gpu-b200`, even though these run on different hardware with different execution times.

## Modifications

- Add `job_name_to_suite()` to extract suite name from CI job names (stripping the partition suffix)
- Key timings by `(filename, suite)` instead of `(filename, backend)`
- Match `est_time` updates by both function name and `suite=` argument, so each registration call gets its own per-suite median

body:
### Motivation
- Root cause: `CaseCardFactory.create(...)` was the single shared decision point and always sourced the background from the responsible-attorney color with no branch for non-engagement cases.  
- Goal: make a top-priority override so cases with `NonEngagementLetterSent == true` render with `#D4D4DFF` app‑wide while preserving existing behavior otherwise.  
- Scope: surgical change at the shared CaseCard factory plus the minimal plumbing to surface the boolean to every place that constructs `CaseCardModel`.

### Description
- Added a top-priority override in `CaseCardFactory.create(...)` that sets `#D4D4DFF` when `vm.nonEngagementLetterSent()` is `true`, otherwise falling back to `ColorUtil.toCssBackgroundColorOrNull(vm.responsibleAttorneyColor())`.  
- Threaded `nonEngagementLetterSent` through the UI VM and factory path by adding it to `CaseCardModel` and the small view-models (`CasesController`, `MyShaleController`, `OrganizationController`, `ContactViewController`, `SearchController`, `UserController`, etc.) so every `CaseCard` construction uses the flag.  
- Added minimal DAO/DTO/query plumbing so the flag is available from data layer: `NonEngagementLetterSent` was included in `CaseDao` projections and in related-case queries in `ContactDao` and `OrganizationDao`, and task-related queries/DTOs were extended so task mini-case previews also carry `caseNonEngagementLetterSent`.  
- Exact files changed (surgical set): `shale-ui/src/main/java/com/shale/ui/component/factory/CaseCardFactory.java`, `shale-ui/src/main/java/com/shale/ui/component/TaskCard.java`, `shale-ui/src/main/java/com/shale/ui/component/factory/TaskCardFactory.java`, `shale-ui/src/main/java/com/shale/ui/component/dialog/TaskDetailDialog.java`, `shale-ui/src/main/java/com/shale/ui/component/dialog/NotificationCenterDialog.java`, `shale-ui/src/main/java/com/shale/ui/component/dialog/TaskDetailDialog.java`, `shale-ui/src/main/java/com/shale/ui/component/dialog/NotificationCenterDialog.java`, controllers: `CasesController`, `MyShaleController`, `SearchController`, `UserController`, `OrganizationController`, `ContactViewController`, `CaseController`, `SceneManager`, and data/core layers: `shale-data/src/main/java/com/shale/data/dao/CaseDao.java`, `ContactDao.java`, `OrganizationDao.java`, `TaskDao.java`, and DTOs `shale-core/src/main/java/com/shale/core/dto/CaseTaskListItemDto.java` and `TaskDetailDto.java`.  
- Before/after (concise): Before, CaseCards always used the responsible-attorney derived background; after, a case with `NonEngagementLetterSent == true` uses `#D4D4DFF` everywhere `CaseCard` is rendered, and `false/null` preserves previous behavior exactly.

### Testing

- No automated UI screenshot tests were run in this environment; the change was kept targeted to background color decision only to avoid layout/interaction regressions.

## Sequence changes
- **Removed:** birthday bubble, "You absolute legend" / emoji burst / "whole crew" messages, second and third gates, airplane SCRIPT beat, map navigation from plane
- **New flow after gate:** `now light your candles 🕯️` → candle challenge (24 taps) → `oh no look out! 😱` → `here comes an airoplane! ✈️` + plane animation → `but wait theres more? 👀` → `open this! 💌` → closed envelope bubble → tap to reveal letter

## Content changes
- **Birthday letter (`mkHeartfeltHTML`):** replaced generic placeholder with Athena's full personal letter to Ali
- **Chess card (`mkChessHTML`):** stripped subtitle copy, now reads "a game for two 🎮"

## New envelope bubble
Added `mkPostBubbleHTML` / `buildPostBubbleWrap` and `.post-bubble` CSS. The bubble renders a floating 💌 with a "tap to open" hint; clicking it marks it `post-opened` (dims, disables pointer-events) and triggers `revealHeartfelt`.

## Airplane refactor
`launchFlyingPlane` now accepts an `onArrived` callback instead of wiring a `click → map.html` handler. Map toasts removed. The callback drives the "but wait theres more?" chain once the plane settles.

## Cleanup
- Deleted unused `mkJokeHTML` and `mkPlaneHTML`
- Removed plane-bubble → `revealHeaderIcon('hdr-map-icon')` side-effect from `appendMsg`
- Removed `planeBeatIdx` map-icon restore logic from `loadState`
